problem:
Here is a workload captured from a production trace:

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Priority |
|---------|---------|-------|----------|
| P1      | 1       | 8     | 5        |
| P2      | 4       | 1     | 2        |
| P3      | 6       | 10    | 5        |
| P4      | 9       | 6     | 4        |
| P5      | 13      | 6     | 3        |
| P6      | 18      | 4     | 5        |
| P7      | 22      | 1     | 1        |
| P8      | 27      | 2     | 4        |

They are scheduled with **Priority (preemptive)** (a lower number means higher priority). Show the schedule step by step and report both averages.
solution:
**Algorithm: Priority (preemptive)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: at every arrival and completion, run the ready process with the HIGHEST priority (LOWEST number); preempt the running process if a higher-priority one is ready (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=1
- t=1: P1 arrives; only P1 is ready -> run P1
- t=4: P2 arrives; ready P2(p2) < P1(p5) -> PREEMPT P1, run P2
- t=5: P2 completes; only P1 is ready -> run P1
- t=6: P3 arrives; ready P1(p5) = P3(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> keep running P1
- t=9: P4 arrives; ready P4(p4) < P1(p5) = P3(p5) -> PREEMPT P1, run P4
- t=13: P5 arrives; ready P5(p3) < P4(p4) < P1(p5) = P3(p5) -> PREEMPT P4, run P5
- t=18: P6 arrives; ready P5(p3) < P4(p4) < P1(p5) = P3(p5) = P6(p5) -> keep running P5
- t=19: P5 completes; ready P4(p4) < P1(p5) = P3(p5) = P6(p5) -> run P4
- t=21: P4 completes; ready P1(p5) = P3(p5) = P6(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P1
- t=22: P1 completes; P7 arrives; ready P7(p1) < P3(p5) = P6(p5) -> run P7
- t=23: P7 completes; ready P3(p5) = P6(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P3
- t=27: P8 arrives; ready P8(p4) < P3(p5) = P6(p5) -> PREEMPT P3, run P8
- t=29: P8 completes; ready P3(p5) = P6(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P3
- t=35: P3 completes; only P6 is ready -> run P6
- t=39: P6 completes; all processes done

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** P1[1-4] P2[4-5] P1[5-9] P4[9-13] P5[13-19] P4[19-21] P1[21-22] P7[22-23] P3[23-27] P8[27-29] P3[29-35] P6[35-39]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround   | Waiting      |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|--------------|--------------|
| P1      | 1       | 8     | 22         | 22 - 1 = 21  | 21 - 8 = 13  |
| P2      | 4       | 1     | 5          | 5 - 4 = 1    | 1 - 1 = 0    |
| P3      | 6       | 10    | 35         | 35 - 6 = 29  | 29 - 10 = 19 |
| P4      | 9       | 6     | 21         | 21 - 9 = 12  | 12 - 6 = 6   |
| P5      | 13      | 6     | 19         | 19 - 13 = 6  | 6 - 6 = 0    |
| P6      | 18      | 4     | 39         | 39 - 18 = 21 | 21 - 4 = 17  |
| P7      | 22      | 1     | 23         | 23 - 22 = 1  | 1 - 1 = 0    |
| P8      | 27      | 2     | 29         | 29 - 27 = 2  | 2 - 2 = 0    |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 13 + 0 = 13, 13 + 19 = 32, 32 + 6 = 38, 38 + 0 = 38, 38 + 17 = 55, 55 + 0 = 55, 55 + 0 = 55
- Average waiting time = 55 / 8 = **6.88**
- Sum of turnaround times: 21 + 1 = 22, 22 + 29 = 51, 51 + 12 = 63, 63 + 6 = 69, 69 + 21 = 90, 90 + 1 = 91, 91 + 2 = 93
- Average turnaround time = 93 / 8 = **11.62**

**Answer: average waiting time = 6.88, average turnaround time = 11.62**

problem:
Reproduce the following schedule from last term's exam paper:

alpha arrives at time 0 and requires 5 units of CPU time; beta arrives at time 3 and requires 6 units of CPU time; gamma arrives at time 3 and requires 3 units of CPU time; delta arrives at time 4 and requires 8 units of CPU time; epsilon arrives at time 7 and requires 6 units of CPU time; zeta arrives at time 11 and requires 4 units of CPU time; eta arrives at time 14 and requires 5 units of CPU time; theta arrives at time 15 and requires 1 units of CPU time; iota arrives at time 15 and requires 3 units of CPU time.

They are scheduled with **Round Robin (q=3)** with a time quantum of 3. Give the completion time of each process.
solution:
**Algorithm: Round Robin (q=3)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: run the process at the HEAD of the queue for up to q = 3 units; processes arriving during a slice join the tail BEFORE the preempted process goes back to the tail._

- t=0-3: run alpha (head of [alpha]) for 3; 5 - 3 = 2 left; arrived beta(t=3), gamma(t=3) -> tail; alpha back to tail -> queue [beta, gamma, alpha]
- t=3-6: run beta (head of [beta, gamma, alpha]) for 3; 6 - 3 = 3 left; arrived delta(t=4) -> tail; beta back to tail -> queue [gamma, alpha, delta, beta]
- t=6-9: run gamma (head of [gamma, alpha, delta, beta]) for 3; 3 - 3 = 0 left; arrived epsilon(t=7) -> tail; gamma DONE at 9 -> queue [alpha, delta, beta, epsilon]
- t=9-11: run alpha (head of [alpha, delta, beta, epsilon]) for 2; 2 - 2 = 0 left; arrived zeta(t=11) -> tail; alpha DONE at 11 -> queue [delta, beta, epsilon, zeta]
- t=11-14: run delta (head of [delta, beta, epsilon, zeta]) for 3; 8 - 3 = 5 left; arrived eta(t=14) -> tail; delta back to tail -> queue [beta, epsilon, zeta, eta, delta]
- t=14-17: run beta (head of [beta, epsilon, zeta, eta, delta]) for 3; 3 - 3 = 0 left; arrived iota(t=15), theta(t=15) -> tail; beta DONE at 17 -> queue [epsilon, zeta, eta, delta, iota, theta]
- t=17-20: run epsilon (head of [epsilon, zeta, eta, delta, iota, theta]) for 3; 6 - 3 = 3 left; epsilon back to tail -> queue [zeta, eta, delta, iota, theta, epsilon]
- t=20-23: run zeta (head of [zeta, eta, delta, iota, theta, epsilon]) for 3; 4 - 3 = 1 left; zeta back to tail -> queue [eta, delta, iota, theta, epsilon, zeta]
- t=23-26: run eta (head of [eta, delta, iota, theta, epsilon, zeta]) for 3; 5 - 3 = 2 left; eta back to tail -> queue [delta, iota, theta, epsilon, zeta, eta]
- t=26-29: run delta (head of [delta, iota, theta, epsilon, zeta, eta]) for 3; 5 - 3 = 2 left; delta back to tail -> queue [iota, theta, epsilon, zeta, eta, delta]
- t=29-32: run iota (head of [iota, theta, epsilon, zeta, eta, delta]) for 3; 3 - 3 = 0 left; iota DONE at 32 -> queue [theta, epsilon, zeta, eta, delta]
- t=32-33: run theta (head of [theta, epsilon, zeta, eta, delta]) for 1; 1 - 1 = 0 left; theta DONE at 33 -> queue [epsilon, zeta, eta, delta]
- t=33-36: run epsilon (head of [epsilon, zeta, eta, delta]) for 3; 3 - 3 = 0 left; epsilon DONE at 36 -> queue [zeta, eta, delta]
- t=36-37: run zeta (head of [zeta, eta, delta]) for 1; 1 - 1 = 0 left; zeta DONE at 37 -> queue [eta, delta]
- t=37-39: run eta (head of [eta, delta]) for 2; 2 - 2 = 0 left; eta DONE at 39 -> queue [delta]
- t=39-41: run delta (head of [delta]) for 2; 2 - 2 = 0 left; delta DONE at 41 -> queue []

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** alpha[0-3] beta[3-6] gamma[6-9] alpha[9-11] delta[11-14] beta[14-17] epsilon[17-20] zeta[20-23] eta[23-26] delta[26-29] iota[29-32] theta[32-33] epsilon[33-36] zeta[36-37] eta[37-39] delta[39-41]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround   | Waiting     |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|--------------|-------------|
| alpha   | 0       | 5     | 11         | 11 - 0 = 11  | 11 - 5 = 6  |
| beta    | 3       | 6     | 17         | 17 - 3 = 14  | 14 - 6 = 8  |
| delta   | 4       | 8     | 41         | 41 - 4 = 37  | 37 - 8 = 29 |
| epsilon | 7       | 6     | 36         | 36 - 7 = 29  | 29 - 6 = 23 |
| eta     | 14      | 5     | 39         | 39 - 14 = 25 | 25 - 5 = 20 |
| gamma   | 3       | 3     | 9          | 9 - 3 = 6    | 6 - 3 = 3   |
| iota    | 15      | 3     | 32         | 32 - 15 = 17 | 17 - 3 = 14 |
| theta   | 15      | 1     | 33         | 33 - 15 = 18 | 18 - 1 = 17 |
| zeta    | 11      | 4     | 37         | 37 - 11 = 26 | 26 - 4 = 22 |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 6 + 8 = 14, 14 + 29 = 43, 43 + 23 = 66, 66 + 20 = 86, 86 + 3 = 89, 89 + 14 = 103, 103 + 17 = 120, 120 + 22 = 142
- Average waiting time = 142 / 9 = **15.78**
- Sum of turnaround times: 11 + 14 = 25, 25 + 37 = 62, 62 + 29 = 91, 91 + 25 = 116, 116 + 6 = 122, 122 + 17 = 139, 139 + 18 = 157, 157 + 26 = 183
- Average turnaround time = 183 / 9 = **20.33**

**Answer: completion times alpha = 11, beta = 17, delta = 41, epsilon = 36, eta = 39, gamma = 9, iota = 32, theta = 33, zeta = 37**

- P1: Need [3, 1, 1] vs Work [0, 5, 2]: 3>0, 1<=5, 1<=2 -> cannot run yet

problem:

Assume **FCFS** scheduling. Construct the Gantt chart, then determine the average waiting and turnaround times.
solution:
**Algorithm: FCFS**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: run processes in order of ARRIVAL; each runs to completion._

- arrival order: P1(t=5), P2(t=11), P3(t=13), P4(t=14), P5(t=15), P6(t=21), P7(t=23), P8(t=25), P9(t=31)

- t=5: P1 runs (arrived t=5, burst 9) -> completes at 5 + 9 = 14
- t=14: P2 runs (arrived t=11, burst 4) -> completes at 14 + 4 = 18
- t=18: P3 runs (arrived t=13, burst 1) -> completes at 18 + 1 = 19
- t=19: P4 runs (arrived t=14, burst 7) -> completes at 19 + 7 = 26
- t=26: P5 runs (arrived t=15, burst 12) -> completes at 26 + 12 = 38
- t=38: P6 runs (arrived t=21, burst 11) -> completes at 38 + 11 = 49
- t=49: P7 runs (arrived t=23, burst 8) -> completes at 49 + 8 = 57
- t=57: P8 runs (arrived t=25, burst 1) -> completes at 57 + 1 = 58
- t=58: P9 runs (arrived t=31, burst 4) -> completes at 58 + 4 = 62

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** P1[5-14] P2[14-18] P3[18-19] P4[19-26] P5[26-38] P6[38-49] P7[49-57] P8[57-58] P9[58-62]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround   | Waiting      |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|--------------|--------------|
| P1      | 5       | 9     | 14         | 14 - 5 = 9   | 9 - 9 = 0    |
| P2      | 11      | 4     | 18         | 18 - 11 = 7  | 7 - 4 = 3    |
| P3      | 13      | 1     | 19         | 19 - 13 = 6  | 6 - 1 = 5    |
| P4      | 14      | 7     | 26         | 26 - 14 = 12 | 12 - 7 = 5   |
| P5      | 15      | 12    | 38         | 38 - 15 = 23 | 23 - 12 = 11 |
| P6      | 21      | 11    | 49         | 49 - 21 = 28 | 28 - 11 = 17 |
| P7      | 23      | 8     | 57         | 57 - 23 = 34 | 34 - 8 = 26  |
| P8      | 25      | 1     | 58         | 58 - 25 = 33 | 33 - 1 = 32  |
| P9      | 31      | 4     | 62         | 62 - 31 = 31 | 31 - 4 = 27  |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 0 + 3 = 3, 3 + 5 = 8, 8 + 5 = 13, 13 + 11 = 24, 24 + 17 = 41, 41 + 26 = 67, 67 + 32 = 99, 99 + 27 = 126
- Average waiting time = 126 / 9 = **14.0**
- Sum of turnaround times: 9 + 7 = 16, 16 + 6 = 22, 22 + 12 = 34, 34 + 23 = 57, 57 + 28 = 85, 85 + 34 = 119, 119 + 33 = 152, 152 + 31 = 183

**Answer: average waiting time = 14.0, average turnaround time = 20.33**

problem:

| P3 | 1       | 0       | 3       | 0       | 1     | 1     | 5     | 2     |

A request of [0, 3, 1, 0] arrives from P0. Can it be satisfied safely?

Your team is reviewing a scheduling trace. The recorded workload was:

alpha arrives at time 4 and requires 2 units of CPU time; beta arrives at time 8 and requires 5 units of CPU time; gamma arrives at time 10 and requires 1 units of CPU time; delta arrives at time 12 and requires 4 units of CPU time; epsilon arrives at time 15 and requires 1 units of CPU time; zeta arrives at time 17 and requires 6 units of CPU time; eta arrives at time 21 and requires 5 units of CPU time; theta arrives at time 22 and requires 1 units of CPU time; iota arrives at time 26 and requires 9 units of CPU time.

The scheduler uses **SJF (non-preemptive)**. Work through the schedule and give the average waiting time, showing all intermediate steps.
solution:
**Algorithm: SJF (non-preemptive)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: whenever the CPU is free, run the ready process with the SHORTEST BURST to completion (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=4
- t=4: only alpha is ready -> run alpha, done at 4 + 2 = 6
- t=6: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=8
- t=8: only beta is ready -> run beta, done at 8 + 5 = 13
- t=13: ready gamma(1) < delta(4) -> run gamma, done at 13 + 1 = 14
- t=14: only delta is ready -> run delta, done at 14 + 4 = 18
- t=18: ready epsilon(1) < zeta(6) -> run epsilon, done at 18 + 1 = 19
- t=19: only zeta is ready -> run zeta, done at 19 + 6 = 25
- t=25: ready theta(1) < eta(5) -> run theta, done at 25 + 1 = 26
- t=26: ready eta(5) < iota(9) -> run eta, done at 26 + 5 = 31
- t=31: only iota is ready -> run iota, done at 31 + 9 = 40

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** alpha[4-6] beta[8-13] gamma[13-14] delta[14-18] epsilon[18-19] zeta[19-25] theta[25-26] eta[26-31] iota[31-40]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround   | Waiting    |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|--------------|------------|
| alpha   | 4       | 2     | 6          | 6 - 4 = 2    | 2 - 2 = 0  |
| beta    | 8       | 5     | 13         | 13 - 8 = 5   | 5 - 5 = 0  |
| delta   | 12      | 4     | 18         | 18 - 12 = 6  | 6 - 4 = 2  |
| epsilon | 15      | 1     | 19         | 19 - 15 = 4  | 4 - 1 = 3  |
| eta     | 21      | 5     | 31         | 31 - 21 = 10 | 10 - 5 = 5 |
| gamma   | 10      | 1     | 14         | 14 - 10 = 4  | 4 - 1 = 3  |
| iota    | 26      | 9     | 40         | 40 - 26 = 14 | 14 - 9 = 5 |
| theta   | 22      | 1     | 26         | 26 - 22 = 4  | 4 - 1 = 3  |
| zeta    | 17      | 6     | 25         | 25 - 17 = 8  | 8 - 6 = 2  |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 0 + 0 = 0, 0 + 2 = 2, 2 + 3 = 5, 5 + 5 = 10, 10 + 3 = 13, 13 + 5 = 18, 18 + 3 = 21, 21 + 2 = 23
- Average waiting time = 23 / 9 = **2.56**
- Sum of turnaround times: 2 + 5 = 7, 7 + 6 = 13, 13 + 4 = 17, 17 + 10 = 27, 27 + 4 = 31, 31 + 14 = 45, 45 + 4 = 49, 49 + 8 = 57
- Average turnaround time = 57 / 9 = **6.33**

**Answer: average waiting time = 2.56**

- Test 2: Request [0, 0, 1] vs Available [4, 1, 6]: 0<=4, 0<=1, 1<=6 -> OK
- Test 3: pretend to grant. Available = [4, 1, 6] - [0, 0, 1] = [4, 1, 5]; Allocation[P3] = [2, 5, 1]. Now run the safety algorithm.

- P2: Need [4, 4, 0] vs Work [5, 1, 5]: 4<=5, 4>1, 0<=5 -> cannot run yet
- P3: Need [0, 3, 0] vs Work [5, 1, 5]: 0<=5, 3>1, 0<=5 -> cannot run yet

- P2: Need [4, 4, 0] vs Work [10, 6, 12]: 4<=10, 4<=6, 0<=12 -> all fit, run it. Work = [10, 6, 12] + Allocation [4, 0, 0] = [14, 6, 12]

- Resulting state is SAFE (sequence < P0, P4, P1, P2, P3, P5 >) -> GRANT the request

**Algorithm: SRTF (preemptive SJF)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: at every arrival and completion, run the ready process with the SHORTEST REMAINING time; preempt the running process if a shorter one is ready (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: alpha, beta arrive; ready alpha(9) < beta(12) -> run alpha

- t=4: delta completes; epsilon, zeta, eta arrive; ready epsilon(3) < gamma(4) = eta(4) < alpha(8) < beta(12) = zeta(12) -> run epsilon
- t=6: theta arrives; ready epsilon(1) < theta(3) < gamma(4) = eta(4) < alpha(8) < beta(12) = zeta(12) -> keep running epsilon
- t=7: epsilon completes; ready theta(3) < gamma(4) = eta(4) < alpha(8) < beta(12) = zeta(12) -> run theta
- t=10: theta completes; ready gamma(4) = eta(4) < alpha(8) < beta(12) = zeta(12) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run gamma
- t=14: gamma completes; ready eta(4) < alpha(8) < beta(12) = zeta(12) -> run eta
- t=18: eta completes; ready alpha(8) < beta(12) = zeta(12) -> run alpha
- t=26: alpha completes; ready beta(12) = zeta(12) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run beta
- t=38: beta completes; only zeta is ready -> run zeta
- t=50: zeta completes; all processes done

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** alpha[0-1] gamma[1-2] delta[2-4] epsilon[4-7] theta[7-10] gamma[10-14] eta[14-18] alpha[18-26] beta[26-38] zeta[38-50]

|---------|---------|-------|------------|-------------|--------------|

| beta    | 0       | 12    | 38         | 38 - 0 = 38 | 38 - 12 = 26 |
| delta   | 2       | 2     | 4          | 4 - 2 = 2   | 2 - 2 = 0    |
| epsilon | 4       | 3     | 7          | 7 - 4 = 3   | 3 - 3 = 0    |
| eta     | 4       | 4     | 18         | 18 - 4 = 14 | 14 - 4 = 10  |
| gamma   | 1       | 5     | 14         | 14 - 1 = 13 | 13 - 5 = 8   |
| theta   | 6       | 3     | 10         | 10 - 6 = 4  | 4 - 3 = 1    |
| zeta    | 4       | 12    | 50         | 50 - 4 = 46 | 46 - 12 = 34 |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 17 + 26 = 43, 43 + 0 = 43, 43 + 0 = 43, 43 + 10 = 53, 53 + 8 = 61, 61 + 1 = 62, 62 + 34 = 96

- Sum of turnaround times: 26 + 38 = 64, 64 + 2 = 66, 66 + 3 = 69, 69 + 14 = 83, 83 + 13 = 96, 96 + 4 = 100, 100 + 46 = 146
- Average turnaround time = 146 / 8 = **18.25**

**Answer: average waiting time = 12.0, average turnaround time = 18.25**

problem:
The allocator's free list currently holds `[161, 124, 120, 291, 591, 546]` KB blocks. The queue asks for `[493, 327, 457, 323, 446, 180]` KB, served first to last.

Allocate these requests with **WORST-fit** and report the leftover space in each hole.
solution:
**Policy: WORST-fit**

_Rule: take the LARGEST hole that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=161, hole 2=124, hole 3=120, hole 4=291, hole 5=591, hole 6=546
- request 493: hole 1=161 < 493 no; hole 2=124 < 493 no; hole 3=120 < 493 no; hole 4=291 < 493 no; hole 5=591 >= 493 fits; hole 6=546 >= 493 fits -> largest fitting: 591 > 546 -> hole 5; 591 - 493 = 98
- request 327: hole 1=161 < 327 no; hole 2=124 < 327 no; hole 3=120 < 327 no; hole 4=291 < 327 no; hole 5=98 < 327 no; hole 6=546 >= 327 fits -> largest fitting: 546 -> hole 6; 546 - 327 = 219
- request 457: hole 1=161 < 457 no; hole 2=124 < 457 no; hole 3=120 < 457 no; hole 4=291 < 457 no; hole 5=98 < 457 no; hole 6=219 < 457 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT
- request 323: hole 1=161 < 323 no; hole 2=124 < 323 no; hole 3=120 < 323 no; hole 4=291 < 323 no; hole 5=98 < 323 no; hole 6=219 < 323 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT
- request 446: hole 1=161 < 446 no; hole 2=124 < 446 no; hole 3=120 < 446 no; hole 4=291 < 446 no; hole 5=98 < 446 no; hole 6=219 < 446 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT
- request 180: hole 1=161 < 180 no; hole 2=124 < 180 no; hole 3=120 < 180 no; hole 4=291 >= 180 fits; hole 5=98 < 180 no; hole 6=219 >= 180 fits -> largest fitting: 291 > 219 -> hole 4; 291 - 180 = 111

**Placement:** 493 KB -> hole 5; 327 KB -> hole 6; 457 KB -> WAIT; 323 KB -> WAIT; 446 KB -> WAIT; 180 KB -> hole 4
**Remaining free space per hole:** [161, 124, 120, 111, 98, 219]
- Sum of free space: 161 + 124 = 285, 285 + 120 = 405, 405 + 111 = 516, 516 + 98 = 614, 614 + 219 = 833
**Total external fragmentation = 833 KB**

**Answer: 493 KB -> hole 5; 327 KB -> hole 6; 457 KB -> WAIT; 323 KB -> WAIT; 446 KB -> WAIT; 180 KB -> hole 4**

problem:
Reproduce the following schedule from last term's exam paper:

T1 arrives at time 0 and requires 1 units of CPU time with priority 2; T2 arrives at time 0 and requires 2 units of CPU time with priority 5; T3 arrives at time 0 and requires 9 units of CPU time with priority 1; T4 arrives at time 0 and requires 6 units of CPU time with priority 2; T5 arrives at time 0 and requires 6 units of CPU time with priority 3; T6 arrives at time 0 and requires 5 units of CPU time with priority 4; T7 arrives at time 0 and requires 7 units of CPU time with priority 2; T8 arrives at time 0 and requires 2 units of CPU time with priority 2.

Use **Priority (non-preemptive)** (a lower number means higher priority). Give the completion time of each process.
solution:
**Algorithm: Priority (non-preemptive)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: whenever the CPU is free, run the ready process with the HIGHEST priority (LOWEST number) to completion (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: ready T3(p1) < T1(p2) = T4(p2) = T7(p2) = T8(p2) < T5(p3) < T6(p4) < T2(p5) -> run T3, done at 0 + 9 = 9
- t=9: ready T1(p2) = T4(p2) = T7(p2) = T8(p2) < T5(p3) < T6(p4) < T2(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run T1, done at 9 + 1 = 10
- t=10: ready T4(p2) = T7(p2) = T8(p2) < T5(p3) < T6(p4) < T2(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run T4, done at 10 + 6 = 16
- t=16: ready T7(p2) = T8(p2) < T5(p3) < T6(p4) < T2(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run T7, done at 16 + 7 = 23
- t=23: ready T8(p2) < T5(p3) < T6(p4) < T2(p5) -> run T8, done at 23 + 2 = 25
- t=25: ready T5(p3) < T6(p4) < T2(p5) -> run T5, done at 25 + 6 = 31
- t=31: ready T6(p4) < T2(p5) -> run T6, done at 31 + 5 = 36
- t=36: only T2 is ready -> run T2, done at 36 + 2 = 38

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** T3[0-9] T1[9-10] T4[10-16] T7[16-23] T8[23-25] T5[25-31] T6[31-36] T2[36-38]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround  | Waiting     |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|-------------|-------------|
| T1      | 0       | 1     | 10         | 10 - 0 = 10 | 10 - 1 = 9  |
| T2      | 0       | 2     | 38         | 38 - 0 = 38 | 38 - 2 = 36 |
| T3      | 0       | 9     | 9          | 9 - 0 = 9   | 9 - 9 = 0   |
| T4      | 0       | 6     | 16         | 16 - 0 = 16 | 16 - 6 = 10 |
| T5      | 0       | 6     | 31         | 31 - 0 = 31 | 31 - 6 = 25 |
| T6      | 0       | 5     | 36         | 36 - 0 = 36 | 36 - 5 = 31 |
| T7      | 0       | 7     | 23         | 23 - 0 = 23 | 23 - 7 = 16 |
| T8      | 0       | 2     | 25         | 25 - 0 = 25 | 25 - 2 = 23 |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 9 + 36 = 45, 45 + 0 = 45, 45 + 10 = 55, 55 + 25 = 80, 80 + 31 = 111, 111 + 16 = 127, 127 + 23 = 150
- Average waiting time = 150 / 8 = **18.75**
- Sum of turnaround times: 10 + 38 = 48, 48 + 9 = 57, 57 + 16 = 73, 73 + 31 = 104, 104 + 36 = 140, 140 + 23 = 163, 163 + 25 = 188
- Average turnaround time = 188 / 8 = **23.5**

**Answer: completion times T1 = 10, T2 = 38, T3 = 9, T4 = 16, T5 = 31, T6 = 36, T7 = 23, T8 = 25**

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=326, hole 2=444, hole 3=484, hole 4=168, hole 5=595, hole 6=272

- request 391: hole 1=202 < 391 no; hole 2=444 >= 391 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 2; 444 - 391 = 53
- request 40: hole 1=202 >= 40 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 1; 202 - 40 = 162
- request 59: hole 1=162 >= 59 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 1; 162 - 59 = 103
- request 56: hole 1=103 >= 56 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 1; 103 - 56 = 47

**Placement:** 124 KB -> hole 1; 391 KB -> hole 2; 40 KB -> hole 1; 59 KB -> hole 1; 56 KB -> hole 1
**Remaining free space per hole:** [47, 53, 484, 168, 595, 272]
- Sum of free space: 47 + 53 = 100, 100 + 484 = 584, 584 + 168 = 752, 752 + 595 = 1347, 1347 + 272 = 1619
**Total external fragmentation = 1619 KB**

**Answer: 124 KB -> hole 1; 391 KB -> hole 2; 40 KB -> hole 1; 59 KB -> hole 1; 56 KB -> hole 1**

**Algorithm: Round Robin (q=4)**

- t=0: queue empty -> CPU idle until t=2

problem:

**Policy: FIRST-fit**

_Rule: scan holes in order and take the FIRST that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=230, hole 2=256, hole 3=324, hole 4=282, hole 5=304, hole 6=276, hole 7=116

- request 76: hole 1=179 >= 76 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 1; 179 - 76 = 103
- request 151: hole 1=103 < 151 no; hole 2=256 >= 151 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 2; 256 - 151 = 105
- request 299: hole 1=103 < 299 no; hole 2=105 < 299 no; hole 3=324 >= 299 fits -> first fitting hole = hole 3; 324 - 299 = 25

**Remaining free space per hole:** [103, 105, 25, 282, 304, 276, 116]
- Sum of free space: 103 + 105 = 208, 208 + 25 = 233, 233 + 282 = 515, 515 + 304 = 819, 819 + 276 = 1095, 1095 + 116 = 1211
**Total external fragmentation = 1211 KB**

**Answer: 51 KB -> hole 1; 470 KB -> WAIT; 76 KB -> hole 1; 151 KB -> hole 2; 299 KB -> hole 3; 404 KB -> WAIT**

problem:
Your team is reviewing a scheduling trace. The recorded workload was:

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Priority |
|---------|---------|-------|----------|
| P1      | 0       | 10    | 1        |
| P2      | 0       | 8     | 4        |
| P3      | 1       | 1     | 3        |
| P4      | 5       | 2     | 2        |
| P5      | 5       | 8     | 5        |
| P6      | 5       | 3     | 2        |
| P7      | 8       | 12    | 2        |
| P8      | 10      | 12    | 4        |

The scheduler uses **Priority (preemptive)** (a lower number means higher priority). Work through the schedule and give the average waiting time, showing all intermediate steps.
solution:
**Algorithm: Priority (preemptive)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: at every arrival and completion, run the ready process with the HIGHEST priority (LOWEST number); preempt the running process if a higher-priority one is ready (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: P1, P2 arrive; ready P1(p1) < P2(p4) -> run P1
- t=1: P3 arrives; ready P1(p1) < P3(p3) < P2(p4) -> keep running P1
- t=5: P4, P5, P6 arrive; ready P1(p1) < P4(p2) = P6(p2) < P3(p3) < P2(p4) < P5(p5) -> keep running P1
- t=8: P7 arrives; ready P1(p1) < P4(p2) = P6(p2) = P7(p2) < P3(p3) < P2(p4) < P5(p5) -> keep running P1
- t=10: P1 completes; P8 arrives; ready P4(p2) = P6(p2) = P7(p2) < P3(p3) < P2(p4) = P8(p4) < P5(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P4
- t=12: P4 completes; ready P6(p2) = P7(p2) < P3(p3) < P2(p4) = P8(p4) < P5(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P6
- t=15: P6 completes; ready P7(p2) < P3(p3) < P2(p4) = P8(p4) < P5(p5) -> run P7
- t=27: P7 completes; ready P3(p3) < P2(p4) = P8(p4) < P5(p5) -> run P3
- t=28: P3 completes; ready P2(p4) = P8(p4) < P5(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P2
- t=36: P2 completes; ready P8(p4) < P5(p5) -> run P8
- t=48: P8 completes; only P5 is ready -> run P5
- t=56: P5 completes; all processes done

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** P1[0-10] P4[10-12] P6[12-15] P7[15-27] P3[27-28] P2[28-36] P8[36-48] P5[48-56]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround   | Waiting      |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|--------------|--------------|
| P1      | 0       | 10    | 10         | 10 - 0 = 10  | 10 - 10 = 0  |
| P2      | 0       | 8     | 36         | 36 - 0 = 36  | 36 - 8 = 28  |
| P3      | 1       | 1     | 28         | 28 - 1 = 27  | 27 - 1 = 26  |
| P4      | 5       | 2     | 12         | 12 - 5 = 7   | 7 - 2 = 5    |
| P5      | 5       | 8     | 56         | 56 - 5 = 51  | 51 - 8 = 43  |
| P6      | 5       | 3     | 15         | 15 - 5 = 10  | 10 - 3 = 7   |
| P7      | 8       | 12    | 27         | 27 - 8 = 19  | 19 - 12 = 7  |
| P8      | 10      | 12    | 48         | 48 - 10 = 38 | 38 - 12 = 26 |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 0 + 28 = 28, 28 + 26 = 54, 54 + 5 = 59, 59 + 43 = 102, 102 + 7 = 109, 109 + 7 = 116, 116 + 26 = 142
- Average waiting time = 142 / 8 = **17.75**
- Sum of turnaround times: 10 + 36 = 46, 46 + 27 = 73, 73 + 7 = 80, 80 + 51 = 131, 131 + 10 = 141, 141 + 19 = 160, 160 + 38 = 198
- Average turnaround time = 198 / 8 = **24.75**

**Answer: average waiting time = 17.75**

problem:
An allocation snapshot from a 3-resource system (A, B, C) with 6 processes: Free instances right now: [0, 6, 0].

| P  | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Max A | Max B | Max C |
|----|---------|---------|---------|-------|-------|-------|
| P1 | 3       | 6       | 0       | 7     | 6     | 6     |
| P2 | 1       | 0       | 1       | 4     | 0     | 6     |
| P3 | 0       | 0       | 6       | 7     | 1     | 8     |
| P4 | 0       | 0       | 0       | 2     | 0     | 5     |
| P5 | 1       | 3       | 7       | 5     | 6     | 8     |
| P6 | 0       | 3       | 1       | 0     | 5     | 6     |

Is this state safe? Apply the safety algorithm and show a safe sequence if one exists.
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C)

- P1: [7, 6, 6] - [3, 6, 0] = [4, 0, 6]
- P2: [4, 0, 6] - [1, 0, 1] = [3, 0, 5]
- P3: [7, 1, 8] - [0, 0, 6] = [7, 1, 2]
- P4: [2, 0, 5] - [0, 0, 0] = [2, 0, 5]
- P5: [5, 6, 8] - [1, 3, 7] = [4, 3, 1]
- P6: [0, 5, 6] - [0, 3, 1] = [0, 2, 5]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [0, 6, 0]
- P1: Need [4, 0, 6] vs Work [0, 6, 0]: 4>0, 0<=6, 6>0 -> cannot run yet
- P2: Need [3, 0, 5] vs Work [0, 6, 0]: 3>0, 0<=6, 5>0 -> cannot run yet
- P3: Need [7, 1, 2] vs Work [0, 6, 0]: 7>0, 1<=6, 2>0 -> cannot run yet
- P4: Need [2, 0, 5] vs Work [0, 6, 0]: 2>0, 0<=6, 5>0 -> cannot run yet
- P5: Need [4, 3, 1] vs Work [0, 6, 0]: 4>0, 3<=6, 1>0 -> cannot run yet
- P6: Need [0, 2, 5] vs Work [0, 6, 0]: 0<=0, 2<=6, 5>0 -> cannot run yet

**Step 3 - conclusion**

No remaining process (P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6) has a Need that fits in Work [0, 6, 0], so they can never all finish: the system is **NOT in a safe state (UNSAFE)**.

_Unsafe does not mean deadlocked yet: it means a deadlock is possible if the processes request their maximum._

**Answer: UNSAFE, no safe sequence exists**

- epsilon: [1, 5, 6, 1] - [0, 2, 1, 1] = [1, 3, 5, 0]
- zeta: [5, 6, 1, 7] - [4, 2, 0, 6] = [1, 4, 1, 1]

**Step 2 - apply the three tests of the resource-request algorithm**

- Test 1: Request [1, 0, 0, 0] vs Need [4, 3, 0, 2]: 1<=4, 0<=3, 0<=0, 0<=2 -> OK
- Test 2: Request [1, 0, 0, 0] vs Available [2, 5, 3, 4]: 1<=2, 0<=5, 0<=3, 0<=4 -> OK

- Work = Available = [1, 5, 3, 4]

- beta: Need [1, 3, 0, 2] vs Work [1, 5, 3, 4]: 1<=1, 3<=5, 0<=3, 2<=4 -> all fit, run it. Work = [1, 5, 3, 4] + Allocation [7, 0, 1, 3] = [8, 5, 4, 7]

- delta: Need [2, 0, 0, 0] vs Work [10, 12, 16, 9]: 2<=10, 0<=12, 0<=16, 0<=9 -> all fit, run it. Work = [10, 12, 16, 9] + Allocation [1, 4, 0, 0] = [11, 16, 16, 9]

- SAFE. Safe sequence: < beta, alpha, gamma, delta, epsilon, zeta >
- Resulting state is SAFE (sequence < beta, alpha, gamma, delta, epsilon, zeta >) -> GRANT the request

problem:
Reproduce the following schedule from last term's exam paper:

- **J1**: arrives at t=6, needs 4 ms of CPU, priority 4
- **J2**: arrives at t=7, needs 11 ms of CPU, priority 5
- **J3**: arrives at t=13, needs 6 ms of CPU, priority 5
- **J4**: arrives at t=14, needs 1 ms of CPU, priority 2
- **J5**: arrives at t=14, needs 1 ms of CPU, priority 2
- **J6**: arrives at t=19, needs 9 ms of CPU, priority 1
- **J7**: arrives at t=19, needs 12 ms of CPU, priority 2

They are scheduled with **Priority (preemptive)** (a lower number means higher priority). Work through the schedule and give the average waiting time, showing all intermediate steps.
solution:
**Algorithm: Priority (preemptive)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: at every arrival and completion, run the ready process with the HIGHEST priority (LOWEST number); preempt the running process if a higher-priority one is ready (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=6
- t=6: J1 arrives; only J1 is ready -> run J1
- t=7: J2 arrives; ready J1(p4) < J2(p5) -> keep running J1
- t=10: J1 completes; only J2 is ready -> run J2
- t=13: J3 arrives; ready J2(p5) = J3(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> keep running J2
- t=14: J4, J5 arrive; ready J4(p2) = J5(p2) < J2(p5) = J3(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> PREEMPT J2, run J4
- t=15: J4 completes; ready J5(p2) < J2(p5) = J3(p5) -> run J5
- t=16: J5 completes; ready J2(p5) = J3(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run J2
- t=19: J6, J7 arrive; ready J6(p1) < J7(p2) < J2(p5) = J3(p5) -> PREEMPT J2, run J6
- t=28: J6 completes; ready J7(p2) < J2(p5) = J3(p5) -> run J7
- t=40: J7 completes; ready J2(p5) = J3(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run J2
- t=44: J2 completes; only J3 is ready -> run J3
- t=50: J3 completes; all processes done

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** J1[6-10] J2[10-14] J4[14-15] J5[15-16] J2[16-19] J6[19-28] J7[28-40] J2[40-44] J3[44-50]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround   | Waiting      |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|--------------|--------------|
| J1      | 6       | 4     | 10         | 10 - 6 = 4   | 4 - 4 = 0    |
| J2      | 7       | 11    | 44         | 44 - 7 = 37  | 37 - 11 = 26 |
| J3      | 13      | 6     | 50         | 50 - 13 = 37 | 37 - 6 = 31  |
| J4      | 14      | 1     | 15         | 15 - 14 = 1  | 1 - 1 = 0    |
| J5      | 14      | 1     | 16         | 16 - 14 = 2  | 2 - 1 = 1    |
| J6      | 19      | 9     | 28         | 28 - 19 = 9  | 9 - 9 = 0    |
| J7      | 19      | 12    | 40         | 40 - 19 = 21 | 21 - 12 = 9  |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 0 + 26 = 26, 26 + 31 = 57, 57 + 0 = 57, 57 + 1 = 58, 58 + 0 = 58, 58 + 9 = 67
- Average waiting time = 67 / 7 = **9.57**
- Sum of turnaround times: 4 + 37 = 41, 41 + 37 = 78, 78 + 1 = 79, 79 + 2 = 81, 81 + 9 = 90, 90 + 21 = 111
- Average turnaround time = 111 / 7 = **15.86**

**Answer: average waiting time = 9.57**

problem:
A memory dump shows free partitions of `[95, 197, 436, 229, 593, 595, 275]` KB. The queue asks for `[67, 131, 95, 184, 488]` KB, served first to last.

Using **WORST-fit**, show which hole serves each request and the remaining free space.
solution:
**Policy: WORST-fit**

_Rule: take the LARGEST hole that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=95, hole 2=197, hole 3=436, hole 4=229, hole 5=593, hole 6=595, hole 7=275
- request 67: hole 1=95 >= 67 fits; hole 2=197 >= 67 fits; hole 3=436 >= 67 fits; hole 4=229 >= 67 fits; hole 5=593 >= 67 fits; hole 6=595 >= 67 fits; hole 7=275 >= 67 fits -> largest fitting: 595 > 593 > 436 > 275 > 229 > 197 > 95 -> hole 6; 595 - 67 = 528
- request 131: hole 1=95 < 131 no; hole 2=197 >= 131 fits; hole 3=436 >= 131 fits; hole 4=229 >= 131 fits; hole 5=593 >= 131 fits; hole 6=528 >= 131 fits; hole 7=275 >= 131 fits -> largest fitting: 593 > 528 > 436 > 275 > 229 > 197 -> hole 5; 593 - 131 = 462
- request 95: hole 1=95 >= 95 fits; hole 2=197 >= 95 fits; hole 3=436 >= 95 fits; hole 4=229 >= 95 fits; hole 5=462 >= 95 fits; hole 6=528 >= 95 fits; hole 7=275 >= 95 fits -> largest fitting: 528 > 462 > 436 > 275 > 229 > 197 > 95 -> hole 6; 528 - 95 = 433
- request 184: hole 1=95 < 184 no; hole 2=197 >= 184 fits; hole 3=436 >= 184 fits; hole 4=229 >= 184 fits; hole 5=462 >= 184 fits; hole 6=433 >= 184 fits; hole 7=275 >= 184 fits -> largest fitting: 462 > 436 > 433 > 275 > 229 > 197 -> hole 5; 462 - 184 = 278
- request 488: hole 1=95 < 488 no; hole 2=197 < 488 no; hole 3=436 < 488 no; hole 4=229 < 488 no; hole 5=278 < 488 no; hole 6=433 < 488 no; hole 7=275 < 488 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT

**Placement:** 67 KB -> hole 6; 131 KB -> hole 5; 95 KB -> hole 6; 184 KB -> hole 5; 488 KB -> WAIT
**Remaining free space per hole:** [95, 197, 436, 229, 278, 433, 275]
- Sum of free space: 95 + 197 = 292, 292 + 436 = 728, 728 + 229 = 957, 957 + 278 = 1235, 1235 + 433 = 1668, 1668 + 275 = 1943
**Total external fragmentation = 1943 KB**

**Answer: 67 KB -> hole 6; 131 KB -> hole 5; 95 KB -> hole 6; 184 KB -> hole 5; 488 KB -> WAIT**

problem:
An allocation snapshot from a 4-resource system (A, B, C, D) with 7 processes: The monitor reports [0, 5, 6, 0] units still unallocated.

| P    | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Alloc D | Max A | Max B | Max C | Max D |
|------|---------|---------|---------|---------|-------|-------|-------|-------|
| 5384 | 4       | 0       | 0       | 2       | 8     | 1     | 1     | 6     |
| 5394 | 3       | 1       | 1       | 0       | 7     | 1     | 1     | 0     |
| 5405 | 0       | 2       | 0       | 0       | 7     | 2     | 3     | 4     |
| 5435 | 1       | 0       | 0       | 5       | 3     | 4     | 4     | 5     |
| 5446 | 0       | 2       | 8       | 2       | 0     | 3     | 8     | 2     |
| 5468 | 0       | 1       | 0       | 1       | 1     | 8     | 0     | 1     |
| 5495 | 0       | 1       | 0       | 1       | 4     | 3     | 1     | 4     |

Using Banker's algorithm, determine whether the system is in a safe state. If it is, give a safe sequence.
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C, D)

- 5384: [8, 1, 1, 6] - [4, 0, 0, 2] = [4, 1, 1, 4]
- 5394: [7, 1, 1, 0] - [3, 1, 1, 0] = [4, 0, 0, 0]
- 5405: [7, 2, 3, 4] - [0, 2, 0, 0] = [7, 0, 3, 4]
- 5435: [3, 4, 4, 5] - [1, 0, 0, 5] = [2, 4, 4, 0]
- 5446: [0, 3, 8, 2] - [0, 2, 8, 2] = [0, 1, 0, 0]
- 5468: [1, 8, 0, 1] - [0, 1, 0, 1] = [1, 7, 0, 0]
- 5495: [4, 3, 1, 4] - [0, 1, 0, 1] = [4, 2, 1, 3]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [0, 5, 6, 0]
- 5384: Need [4, 1, 1, 4] vs Work [0, 5, 6, 0]: 4>0, 1<=5, 1<=6, 4>0 -> cannot run yet
- 5394: Need [4, 0, 0, 0] vs Work [0, 5, 6, 0]: 4>0, 0<=5, 0<=6, 0<=0 -> cannot run yet
- 5405: Need [7, 0, 3, 4] vs Work [0, 5, 6, 0]: 7>0, 0<=5, 3<=6, 4>0 -> cannot run yet
- 5435: Need [2, 4, 4, 0] vs Work [0, 5, 6, 0]: 2>0, 4<=5, 4<=6, 0<=0 -> cannot run yet
- 5446: Need [0, 1, 0, 0] vs Work [0, 5, 6, 0]: 0<=0, 1<=5, 0<=6, 0<=0 -> all fit, run it. Work = [0, 5, 6, 0] + Allocation [0, 2, 8, 2] = [0, 7, 14, 2]
- 5384: Need [4, 1, 1, 4] vs Work [0, 7, 14, 2]: 4>0, 1<=7, 1<=14, 4>2 -> cannot run yet
- 5394: Need [4, 0, 0, 0] vs Work [0, 7, 14, 2]: 4>0, 0<=7, 0<=14, 0<=2 -> cannot run yet
- 5405: Need [7, 0, 3, 4] vs Work [0, 7, 14, 2]: 7>0, 0<=7, 3<=14, 4>2 -> cannot run yet
- 5435: Need [2, 4, 4, 0] vs Work [0, 7, 14, 2]: 2>0, 4<=7, 4<=14, 0<=2 -> cannot run yet
- 5468: Need [1, 7, 0, 0] vs Work [0, 7, 14, 2]: 1>0, 7<=7, 0<=14, 0<=2 -> cannot run yet
- 5495: Need [4, 2, 1, 3] vs Work [0, 7, 14, 2]: 4>0, 2<=7, 1<=14, 3>2 -> cannot run yet

**Step 3 - conclusion**

No remaining process (5384, 5394, 5405, 5435, 5468, 5495) has a Need that fits in Work [0, 7, 14, 2], so they can never all finish: the system is **NOT in a safe state (UNSAFE)**. Processes 5446 could finish, but 5384, 5394, 5405, 5435, 5468, 5495 cannot.

_Unsafe does not mean deadlocked yet: it means a deadlock is possible if the processes request their maximum._

**Answer: UNSAFE, no safe sequence exists**

problem:
Disk telemetry reports the arm at **135** (device spans 0-199) and a queue of:

`187, 32, 54, 182, 105, 175, 15, 147, 109, 138, 6`

Using **LOOK** scheduling. The head is currently moving toward higher cylinder numbers. Determine the seek sequence and total head movement.
solution:
**Policy: LOOK**

- sorted requests: [6, 15, 32, 54, 105, 109, 138, 147, 175, 182, 187]; below head 135: [6, 15, 32, 54, 105, 109]; at/above head: [138, 147, 175, 182, 187]
- LOOK, head moving UP, towards higher cylinders: service [138, 147, 175, 182, 187], reverse at the last request (not the edge), then service [109, 105, 54, 32, 15, 6]
- 135 -> 138: 138 - 135 = 3; running total 0 + 3 = 3
- 138 -> 147: 147 - 138 = 9; running total 3 + 9 = 12
- 147 -> 175: 175 - 147 = 28; running total 12 + 28 = 40
- 175 -> 182: 182 - 175 = 7; running total 40 + 7 = 47
- 182 -> 187: 187 - 182 = 5; running total 47 + 5 = 52
- 187 -> 109: 187 - 109 = 78; running total 52 + 78 = 130
- 109 -> 105: 109 - 105 = 4; running total 130 + 4 = 134
- 105 -> 54: 105 - 54 = 51; running total 134 + 51 = 185
- 54 -> 32: 54 - 32 = 22; running total 185 + 22 = 207
- 32 -> 15: 32 - 15 = 17; running total 207 + 17 = 224
- 15 -> 6: 15 - 6 = 9; running total 224 + 9 = 233

**Service order:** 138 -> 147 -> 175 -> 182 -> 187 -> 109 -> 105 -> 54 -> 32 -> 15 -> 6
**Total head movement = 233 cylinders**
- Average seek length = 233 / 11 = 21.18

**Answer: total head movement = 233 cylinders**

|---|---------|---------|---------|-------|-------|-------|
| A | 2       | 1       | 0       | 3     | 1     | 0     |
| B | 1       | 4       | 5       | 3     | 7     | 6     |
| C | 4       | 1       | 5       | 5     | 3     | 5     |
| D | 0       | 0       | 0       | 2     | 0     | 7     |
| E | 0       | 0       | 7       | 0     | 1     | 7     |
| F | 0       | 0       | 3       | 3     | 6     | 7     |

Is this state safe? Apply the safety algorithm and show a safe sequence if one exists.
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C)

- A: [3, 1, 0] - [2, 1, 0] = [1, 0, 0]
- B: [3, 7, 6] - [1, 4, 5] = [2, 3, 1]
- C: [5, 3, 5] - [4, 1, 5] = [1, 2, 0]
- D: [2, 0, 7] - [0, 0, 0] = [2, 0, 7]
- E: [0, 1, 7] - [0, 0, 7] = [0, 1, 0]
- F: [3, 6, 7] - [0, 0, 3] = [3, 6, 4]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [4, 4, 6]
- A: Need [1, 0, 0] vs Work [4, 4, 6]: 1<=4, 0<=4, 0<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 4, 6] + Allocation [2, 1, 0] = [6, 5, 6]
- B: Need [2, 3, 1] vs Work [6, 5, 6]: 2<=6, 3<=5, 1<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [6, 5, 6] + Allocation [1, 4, 5] = [7, 9, 11]
- C: Need [1, 2, 0] vs Work [7, 9, 11]: 1<=7, 2<=9, 0<=11 -> all fit, run it. Work = [7, 9, 11] + Allocation [4, 1, 5] = [11, 10, 16]
- D: Need [2, 0, 7] vs Work [11, 10, 16]: 2<=11, 0<=10, 7<=16 -> all fit, run it. Work = [11, 10, 16] + Allocation [0, 0, 0] = [11, 10, 16]
- E: Need [0, 1, 0] vs Work [11, 10, 16]: 0<=11, 1<=10, 0<=16 -> all fit, run it. Work = [11, 10, 16] + Allocation [0, 0, 7] = [11, 10, 23]
- F: Need [3, 6, 4] vs Work [11, 10, 23]: 3<=11, 6<=10, 4<=23 -> all fit, run it. Work = [11, 10, 23] + Allocation [0, 0, 3] = [11, 10, 26]

**Step 3 - conclusion**

All 6 processes can complete, so the system is in a **SAFE state**.
A safe sequence is **< A, B, C, D, E, F >**.

_Safe sequences are not unique: any ordering in which each process's Need is met by the running Work vector is equally correct._

**Answer: SAFE, safe sequence < A, B, C, D, E, F >**

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [1, 4, 6]
- P0: Need [2, 0, 1] vs Work [1, 4, 6]: 2>1, 0<=4, 1<=6 -> cannot run yet
- P1: Need [7, 0, 7] vs Work [1, 4, 6]: 7>1, 0<=4, 7>6 -> cannot run yet
- P2: Need [1, 3, 1] vs Work [1, 4, 6]: 1<=1, 3<=4, 1<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [1, 4, 6] + Allocation [3, 3, 1] = [4, 7, 7]
- P0: Need [2, 0, 1] vs Work [4, 7, 7]: 2<=4, 0<=7, 1<=7 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 7, 7] + Allocation [0, 8, 6] = [4, 15, 13]
- P1: Need [7, 0, 7] vs Work [4, 15, 13]: 7>4, 0<=15, 7<=13 -> cannot run yet
- P3: Need [1, 4, 2] vs Work [4, 15, 13]: 1<=4, 4<=15, 2<=13 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 15, 13] + Allocation [0, 1, 5] = [4, 16, 18]
- P1: Need [7, 0, 7] vs Work [4, 16, 18]: 7>4, 0<=16, 7<=18 -> cannot run yet
- P4: Need [0, 1, 8] vs Work [4, 16, 18]: 0<=4, 1<=16, 8<=18 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 16, 18] + Allocation [4, 0, 0] = [8, 16, 18]
- P1: Need [7, 0, 7] vs Work [8, 16, 18]: 7<=8, 0<=16, 7<=18 -> all fit, run it. Work = [8, 16, 18] + Allocation [1, 0, 1] = [9, 16, 19]
- P5: Need [1, 4, 0] vs Work [9, 16, 19]: 1<=9, 4<=16, 0<=19 -> all fit, run it. Work = [9, 16, 19] + Allocation [2, 2, 3] = [11, 18, 22]

**Step 3 - conclusion**

All 6 processes can complete, so the system is in a **SAFE state**.
A safe sequence is **< P2, P0, P3, P4, P1, P5 >**.

_Safe sequences are not unique: any ordering in which each process's Need is met by the running Work vector is equally correct._

**Answer: SAFE, safe sequence < P2, P0, P3, P4, P1, P5 >**

problem:
Here is a workload captured from a production trace:

alpha arrives at time 5 and requires 4 units of CPU time; beta arrives at time 8 and requires 11 units of CPU time; gamma arrives at time 13 and requires 8 units of CPU time; delta arrives at time 17 and requires 9 units of CPU time; epsilon arrives at time 22 and requires 6 units of CPU time; zeta arrives at time 26 and requires 8 units of CPU time; eta arrives at time 26 and requires 9 units of CPU time; theta arrives at time 30 and requires 6 units of CPU time; iota arrives at time 35 and requires 9 units of CPU time; kappa arrives at time 37 and requires 11 units of CPU time.

Assume **HRRN (highest response ratio next)** scheduling. Give the completion time of each process.
solution:
**Algorithm: HRRN (highest response ratio next)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: whenever the CPU is free, compute each ready process's response ratio = (waiting + burst) / burst and run the HIGHEST ratio to completion (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=5
- t=5: only alpha is ready -> run alpha, done at 5 + 4 = 9
- t=9: only beta is ready -> run beta, done at 9 + 11 = 20
- t=20: ratios: gamma waited 20 - 13 = 7, (7 + 8) / 8 = 1.88, delta waited 20 - 17 = 3, (3 + 9) / 9 = 1.33; order gamma(1.88) > delta(1.33) -> run gamma, done at 20 + 8 = 28
- t=28: ratios: delta waited 28 - 17 = 11, (11 + 9) / 9 = 2.22, epsilon waited 28 - 22 = 6, (6 + 6) / 6 = 2.00, eta waited 28 - 26 = 2, (2 + 9) / 9 = 1.22, zeta waited 28 - 26 = 2, (2 + 8) / 8 = 1.25; order delta(2.22) > epsilon(2.00) > zeta(1.25) > eta(1.22) -> run delta, done at 28 + 9 = 37
- t=37: ratios: epsilon waited 37 - 22 = 15, (15 + 6) / 6 = 3.50, eta waited 37 - 26 = 11, (11 + 9) / 9 = 2.22, zeta waited 37 - 26 = 11, (11 + 8) / 8 = 2.38, theta waited 37 - 30 = 7, (7 + 6) / 6 = 2.17, iota waited 37 - 35 = 2, (2 + 9) / 9 = 1.22, kappa waited 37 - 37 = 0, (0 + 11) / 11 = 1.00; order epsilon(3.50) > zeta(2.38) > eta(2.22) > theta(2.17) > iota(1.22) > kappa(1.00) -> run epsilon, done at 37 + 6 = 43
- t=43: ratios: eta waited 43 - 26 = 17, (17 + 9) / 9 = 2.89, zeta waited 43 - 26 = 17, (17 + 8) / 8 = 3.12, theta waited 43 - 30 = 13, (13 + 6) / 6 = 3.17, iota waited 43 - 35 = 8, (8 + 9) / 9 = 1.89, kappa waited 43 - 37 = 6, (6 + 11) / 11 = 1.55; order theta(3.17) > zeta(3.12) > eta(2.89) > iota(1.89) > kappa(1.55) -> run theta, done at 43 + 6 = 49
- t=49: ratios: eta waited 49 - 26 = 23, (23 + 9) / 9 = 3.56, zeta waited 49 - 26 = 23, (23 + 8) / 8 = 3.88, iota waited 49 - 35 = 14, (14 + 9) / 9 = 2.56, kappa waited 49 - 37 = 12, (12 + 11) / 11 = 2.09; order zeta(3.88) > eta(3.56) > iota(2.56) > kappa(2.09) -> run zeta, done at 49 + 8 = 57
- t=57: ratios: eta waited 57 - 26 = 31, (31 + 9) / 9 = 4.44, iota waited 57 - 35 = 22, (22 + 9) / 9 = 3.44, kappa waited 57 - 37 = 20, (20 + 11) / 11 = 2.82; order eta(4.44) > iota(3.44) > kappa(2.82) -> run eta, done at 57 + 9 = 66
- t=66: ratios: iota waited 66 - 35 = 31, (31 + 9) / 9 = 4.44, kappa waited 66 - 37 = 29, (29 + 11) / 11 = 3.64; order iota(4.44) > kappa(3.64) -> run iota, done at 66 + 9 = 75
- t=75: only kappa is ready -> run kappa, done at 75 + 11 = 86

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** alpha[5-9] beta[9-20] gamma[20-28] delta[28-37] epsilon[37-43] theta[43-49] zeta[49-57] eta[57-66] iota[66-75] kappa[75-86]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround   | Waiting      |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|--------------|--------------|
| alpha   | 5       | 4     | 9          | 9 - 5 = 4    | 4 - 4 = 0    |

| delta   | 17      | 9     | 37         | 37 - 17 = 20 | 20 - 9 = 11  |
| epsilon | 22      | 6     | 43         | 43 - 22 = 21 | 21 - 6 = 15  |
| eta     | 26      | 9     | 66         | 66 - 26 = 40 | 40 - 9 = 31  |
| gamma   | 13      | 8     | 28         | 28 - 13 = 15 | 15 - 8 = 7   |
| iota    | 35      | 9     | 75         | 75 - 35 = 40 | 40 - 9 = 31  |
| kappa   | 37      | 11    | 86         | 86 - 37 = 49 | 49 - 11 = 38 |
| theta   | 30      | 6     | 49         | 49 - 30 = 19 | 19 - 6 = 13  |
| zeta    | 26      | 8     | 57         | 57 - 26 = 31 | 31 - 8 = 23  |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 0 + 1 = 1, 1 + 11 = 12, 12 + 15 = 27, 27 + 31 = 58, 58 + 7 = 65, 65 + 31 = 96, 96 + 38 = 134, 134 + 13 = 147, 147 + 23 = 170
- Average waiting time = 170 / 10 = **17.0**
- Sum of turnaround times: 4 + 12 = 16, 16 + 20 = 36, 36 + 21 = 57, 57 + 40 = 97, 97 + 15 = 112, 112 + 40 = 152, 152 + 49 = 201, 201 + 19 = 220, 220 + 31 = 251
- Average turnaround time = 251 / 10 = **25.1**

**Answer: completion times alpha = 9, beta = 20, delta = 37, epsilon = 43, eta = 66, gamma = 28, iota = 75, kappa = 86, theta = 49, zeta = 57**

problem:
A storage trace shows the head at cylinder **225** on a 250-cylinder device, with these outstanding requests:

`99, 214, 224, 173, 106, 181, 230, 20, 63, 17, 48, 186`

Using **CLOOK** scheduling. The head is currently moving toward lower cylinder numbers. What is the total number of cylinders the head traverses? Show the order.
solution:
**Policy: CLOOK**

- sorted requests: [17, 20, 48, 63, 99, 106, 173, 181, 186, 214, 224, 230]; below head 225: [17, 20, 48, 63, 99, 106, 173, 181, 186, 214, 224]; at/above head: [230]
- C-LOOK, head moving DOWN, towards cylinder 0: service [224, 214, 186, 181, 173, 106, 99, 63, 48, 20, 17], jump to the farthest pending request, continue down through [230]
- 225 -> 224: 225 - 224 = 1; running total 0 + 1 = 1
- 224 -> 214: 224 - 214 = 10; running total 1 + 10 = 11
- 214 -> 186: 214 - 186 = 28; running total 11 + 28 = 39
- 186 -> 181: 186 - 181 = 5; running total 39 + 5 = 44
- 181 -> 173: 181 - 173 = 8; running total 44 + 8 = 52
- 173 -> 106: 173 - 106 = 67; running total 52 + 67 = 119
- 106 -> 99: 106 - 99 = 7; running total 119 + 7 = 126
- 99 -> 63: 99 - 63 = 36; running total 126 + 36 = 162
- 63 -> 48: 63 - 48 = 15; running total 162 + 15 = 177
- 48 -> 20: 48 - 20 = 28; running total 177 + 28 = 205
- 20 -> 17: 20 - 17 = 3; running total 205 + 3 = 208
- 17 -> 230: 230 - 17 = 213; running total 208 + 213 = 421

**Service order:** 224 -> 214 -> 186 -> 181 -> 173 -> 106 -> 99 -> 63 -> 48 -> 20 -> 17 -> 230
**Total head movement = 421 cylinders**
- Average seek length = 421 / 12 = 35.08
- _Convention: this total counts the return jump of 213 cylinders. If your course excludes the jump, the total is 421 - 213 = 208._

**Answer: total head movement = 421 cylinders**

problem:
A storage trace shows the head at cylinder **121** on a 200-cylinder device, with these outstanding requests:

`34, 41, 194, 114, 180, 27, 107, 182, 166, 86, 43, 6`

Using **FCFS** scheduling. List the order in which requests are served and compute the total distance moved.

The allocator's free list currently holds `[548, 257, 390, 75, 194, 578, 149, 388]` KB blocks. The queue asks for `[190, 375, 437, 165, 422, 77]` KB, served first to last.

Apply **WORST-fit** allocation. Which partition serves each request?
solution:
**Policy: WORST-fit**

_Rule: take the LARGEST hole that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=548, hole 2=257, hole 3=390, hole 4=75, hole 5=194, hole 6=578, hole 7=149, hole 8=388
- request 190: hole 1=548 >= 190 fits; hole 2=257 >= 190 fits; hole 3=390 >= 190 fits; hole 4=75 < 190 no; hole 5=194 >= 190 fits; hole 6=578 >= 190 fits; hole 7=149 < 190 no; hole 8=388 >= 190 fits -> largest fitting: 578 > 548 > 390 > 388 > 257 > 194 -> hole 6; 578 - 190 = 388
- request 375: hole 1=548 >= 375 fits; hole 2=257 < 375 no; hole 3=390 >= 375 fits; hole 4=75 < 375 no; hole 5=194 < 375 no; hole 6=388 >= 375 fits; hole 7=149 < 375 no; hole 8=388 >= 375 fits -> largest fitting: 548 > 390 > 388 > 388 -> hole 1; 548 - 375 = 173
- request 437: hole 1=173 < 437 no; hole 2=257 < 437 no; hole 3=390 < 437 no; hole 4=75 < 437 no; hole 5=194 < 437 no; hole 6=388 < 437 no; hole 7=149 < 437 no; hole 8=388 < 437 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT
- request 165: hole 1=173 >= 165 fits; hole 2=257 >= 165 fits; hole 3=390 >= 165 fits; hole 4=75 < 165 no; hole 5=194 >= 165 fits; hole 6=388 >= 165 fits; hole 7=149 < 165 no; hole 8=388 >= 165 fits -> largest fitting: 390 > 388 > 388 > 257 > 194 > 173 -> hole 3; 390 - 165 = 225
- request 422: hole 1=173 < 422 no; hole 2=257 < 422 no; hole 3=225 < 422 no; hole 4=75 < 422 no; hole 5=194 < 422 no; hole 6=388 < 422 no; hole 7=149 < 422 no; hole 8=388 < 422 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT
- request 77: hole 1=173 >= 77 fits; hole 2=257 >= 77 fits; hole 3=225 >= 77 fits; hole 4=75 < 77 no; hole 5=194 >= 77 fits; hole 6=388 >= 77 fits; hole 7=149 >= 77 fits; hole 8=388 >= 77 fits -> largest fitting: 388 > 388 > 257 > 225 > 194 > 173 > 149 -> hole 6; 388 - 77 = 311

**Placement:** 190 KB -> hole 6; 375 KB -> hole 1; 437 KB -> WAIT; 165 KB -> hole 3; 422 KB -> WAIT; 77 KB -> hole 6
**Remaining free space per hole:** [173, 257, 225, 75, 194, 311, 149, 388]
- Sum of free space: 173 + 257 = 430, 430 + 225 = 655, 655 + 75 = 730, 730 + 194 = 924, 924 + 311 = 1235, 1235 + 149 = 1384, 1384 + 388 = 1772
**Total external fragmentation = 1772 KB**

**Answer: 190 KB -> hole 6; 375 KB -> hole 1; 437 KB -> WAIT; 165 KB -> hole 3; 422 KB -> WAIT; 77 KB -> hole 6**

Determine safety using Banker's algorithm, showing the Need matrix and each Work update.
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C, D)

- P0: [1, 3, 5, 0] - [1, 1, 1, 0] = [0, 2, 4, 0]
- P1: [7, 1, 1, 3] - [2, 1, 1, 2] = [5, 0, 0, 1]
- P2: [2, 2, 1, 1] - [2, 1, 0, 0] = [0, 1, 1, 1]
- P3: [3, 7, 4, 2] - [3, 7, 2, 1] = [0, 0, 2, 1]
- P4: [4, 3, 1, 1] - [4, 0, 0, 0] = [0, 3, 1, 1]
- P5: [1, 1, 8, 4] - [1, 1, 3, 3] = [0, 0, 5, 1]
- P6: [6, 0, 8, 7] - [6, 0, 7, 0] = [0, 0, 1, 7]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [1, 6, 5, 4]
- P0: Need [0, 2, 4, 0] vs Work [1, 6, 5, 4]: 0<=1, 2<=6, 4<=5, 0<=4 -> all fit, run it. Work = [1, 6, 5, 4] + Allocation [1, 1, 1, 0] = [2, 7, 6, 4]
- P1: Need [5, 0, 0, 1] vs Work [2, 7, 6, 4]: 5>2, 0<=7, 0<=6, 1<=4 -> cannot run yet
- P2: Need [0, 1, 1, 1] vs Work [2, 7, 6, 4]: 0<=2, 1<=7, 1<=6, 1<=4 -> all fit, run it. Work = [2, 7, 6, 4] + Allocation [2, 1, 0, 0] = [4, 8, 6, 4]
- P1: Need [5, 0, 0, 1] vs Work [4, 8, 6, 4]: 5>4, 0<=8, 0<=6, 1<=4 -> cannot run yet
- P3: Need [0, 0, 2, 1] vs Work [4, 8, 6, 4]: 0<=4, 0<=8, 2<=6, 1<=4 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 8, 6, 4] + Allocation [3, 7, 2, 1] = [7, 15, 8, 5]
- P1: Need [5, 0, 0, 1] vs Work [7, 15, 8, 5]: 5<=7, 0<=15, 0<=8, 1<=5 -> all fit, run it. Work = [7, 15, 8, 5] + Allocation [2, 1, 1, 2] = [9, 16, 9, 7]
- P4: Need [0, 3, 1, 1] vs Work [9, 16, 9, 7]: 0<=9, 3<=16, 1<=9, 1<=7 -> all fit, run it. Work = [9, 16, 9, 7] + Allocation [4, 0, 0, 0] = [13, 16, 9, 7]
- P5: Need [0, 0, 5, 1] vs Work [13, 16, 9, 7]: 0<=13, 0<=16, 5<=9, 1<=7 -> all fit, run it. Work = [13, 16, 9, 7] + Allocation [1, 1, 3, 3] = [14, 17, 12, 10]
- P6: Need [0, 0, 1, 7] vs Work [14, 17, 12, 10]: 0<=14, 0<=17, 1<=12, 7<=10 -> all fit, run it. Work = [14, 17, 12, 10] + Allocation [6, 0, 7, 0] = [20, 17, 19, 10]

**Step 3 - conclusion**

All 7 processes can complete, so the system is in a **SAFE state**.
A safe sequence is **< P0, P2, P3, P1, P4, P5, P6 >**.

_Safe sequences are not unique: any ordering in which each process's Need is met by the running Work vector is equally correct._

**Answer: SAFE, safe sequence < P0, P2, P3, P1, P4, P5, P6 >**

problem:
A colleague sketched this workload on a whiteboard:

- **P1**: arrives at t=1, needs 6 ms of CPU, priority 3
- **P2**: arrives at t=1, needs 9 ms of CPU, priority 1
- **P3**: arrives at t=6, needs 7 ms of CPU, priority 5
- **P4**: arrives at t=6, needs 11 ms of CPU, priority 5
- **P5**: arrives at t=8, needs 11 ms of CPU, priority 3
- **P6**: arrives at t=13, needs 3 ms of CPU, priority 5
- **P7**: arrives at t=14, needs 9 ms of CPU, priority 4
- **P8**: arrives at t=20, needs 2 ms of CPU, priority 2
- **P9**: arrives at t=24, needs 1 ms of CPU, priority 5

Assume **Priority (preemptive)** scheduling (a lower number means higher priority). Draw the Gantt chart showing the execution order.
solution:
**Algorithm: Priority (preemptive)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: at every arrival and completion, run the ready process with the HIGHEST priority (LOWEST number); preempt the running process if a higher-priority one is ready (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=1
- t=1: P1, P2 arrive; ready P2(p1) < P1(p3) -> run P2
- t=6: P3, P4 arrive; ready P2(p1) < P1(p3) < P3(p5) = P4(p5) -> keep running P2
- t=8: P5 arrives; ready P2(p1) < P1(p3) = P5(p3) < P3(p5) = P4(p5) -> keep running P2
- t=10: P2 completes; ready P1(p3) = P5(p3) < P3(p5) = P4(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P1
- t=13: P6 arrives; ready P1(p3) = P5(p3) < P3(p5) = P4(p5) = P6(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> keep running P1
- t=14: P7 arrives; ready P1(p3) = P5(p3) < P7(p4) < P3(p5) = P4(p5) = P6(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> keep running P1
- t=16: P1 completes; ready P5(p3) < P7(p4) < P3(p5) = P4(p5) = P6(p5) -> run P5
- t=20: P8 arrives; ready P8(p2) < P5(p3) < P7(p4) < P3(p5) = P4(p5) = P6(p5) -> PREEMPT P5, run P8
- t=22: P8 completes; ready P5(p3) < P7(p4) < P3(p5) = P4(p5) = P6(p5) -> run P5
- t=24: P9 arrives; ready P5(p3) < P7(p4) < P3(p5) = P4(p5) = P6(p5) = P9(p5) -> keep running P5
- t=29: P5 completes; ready P7(p4) < P3(p5) = P4(p5) = P6(p5) = P9(p5) -> run P7
- t=38: P7 completes; ready P3(p5) = P4(p5) = P6(p5) = P9(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P3
- t=45: P3 completes; ready P4(p5) = P6(p5) = P9(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P4
- t=56: P4 completes; ready P6(p5) = P9(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P6
- t=59: P6 completes; only P9 is ready -> run P9
- t=60: P9 completes; all processes done

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** P2[1-10] P1[10-16] P5[16-20] P8[20-22] P5[22-29] P7[29-38] P3[38-45] P4[45-56] P6[56-59] P9[59-60]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround   | Waiting      |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|--------------|--------------|
| P1      | 1       | 6     | 16         | 16 - 1 = 15  | 15 - 6 = 9   |
| P2      | 1       | 9     | 10         | 10 - 1 = 9   | 9 - 9 = 0    |
| P3      | 6       | 7     | 45         | 45 - 6 = 39  | 39 - 7 = 32  |
| P4      | 6       | 11    | 56         | 56 - 6 = 50  | 50 - 11 = 39 |
| P5      | 8       | 11    | 29         | 29 - 8 = 21  | 21 - 11 = 10 |
| P6      | 13      | 3     | 59         | 59 - 13 = 46 | 46 - 3 = 43  |
| P7      | 14      | 9     | 38         | 38 - 14 = 24 | 24 - 9 = 15  |
| P8      | 20      | 2     | 22         | 22 - 20 = 2  | 2 - 2 = 0    |
| P9      | 24      | 1     | 60         | 60 - 24 = 36 | 36 - 1 = 35  |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 9 + 0 = 9, 9 + 32 = 41, 41 + 39 = 80, 80 + 10 = 90, 90 + 43 = 133, 133 + 15 = 148, 148 + 0 = 148, 148 + 35 = 183
- Average waiting time = 183 / 9 = **20.33**
- Sum of turnaround times: 15 + 9 = 24, 24 + 39 = 63, 63 + 50 = 113, 113 + 21 = 134, 134 + 46 = 180, 180 + 24 = 204, 204 + 2 = 206, 206 + 36 = 242
- Average turnaround time = 242 / 9 = **26.89**

**Answer: Gantt chart P2[1-10] P1[10-16] P5[16-20] P8[20-22] P5[22-29] P7[29-38] P3[38-45] P4[45-56] P6[56-59] P9[59-60]**

problem:

| P  | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Max A | Max B | Max C |
|----|---------|---------|---------|-------|-------|-------|
| P0 | 2       | 0       | 0       | 3     | 3     | 0     |
| P1 | 1       | 0       | 0       | 5     | 1     | 0     |
| P2 | 3       | 1       | 2       | 7     | 2     | 2     |
| P3 | 1       | 4       | 3       | 1     | 5     | 3     |
| P4 | 0       | 1       | 0       | 4     | 8     | 5     |
| P5 | 2       | 3       | 0       | 8     | 8     | 2     |

Process P3 now requests [1, 1, 0]. Should this request be granted?
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C)

- P0: [3, 3, 0] - [2, 0, 0] = [1, 3, 0]
- P1: [5, 1, 0] - [1, 0, 0] = [4, 1, 0]
- P2: [7, 2, 2] - [3, 1, 2] = [4, 1, 0]
- P3: [1, 5, 3] - [1, 4, 3] = [0, 1, 0]
- P4: [4, 8, 5] - [0, 1, 0] = [4, 7, 5]
- P5: [8, 8, 2] - [2, 3, 0] = [6, 5, 2]

**Step 2 - apply the three tests of the resource-request algorithm**

- Test 1 FAILS: Request [1, 1, 0] vs Need [0, 1, 0]: 1>0, 1<=1, 0<=0 -> request exceeds Need for P3 -> error, the process has exceeded its declared maximum

**Conclusion: the request is DENIED.**

**Answer: DENIED**

problem:

| T3 | 2       | 3       | 0       | 8     | 3     | 8     |
| T4 | 2       | 0       | 1       | 4     | 0     | 2     |
| T5 | 0       | 0       | 3       | 3     | 2     | 3     |
| T6 | 5       | 1       | 0       | 5     | 1     | 1     |

Process T5 now requests [0, 1, 0]. Should this request be granted?
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C)

- T1: [1, 2, 6] - [0, 2, 2] = [1, 0, 4]
- T2: [8, 0, 0] - [8, 0, 0] = [0, 0, 0]
- T3: [8, 3, 8] - [2, 3, 0] = [6, 0, 8]
- T4: [4, 0, 2] - [2, 0, 1] = [2, 0, 1]
- T5: [3, 2, 3] - [0, 0, 3] = [3, 2, 0]
- T6: [5, 1, 1] - [5, 1, 0] = [0, 0, 1]

**Step 2 - apply the three tests of the resource-request algorithm**

- Test 1: Request [0, 1, 0] vs Need [3, 2, 0]: 0<=3, 1<=2, 0<=0 -> OK
- Test 2: Request [0, 1, 0] vs Available [5, 1, 6]: 0<=5, 1<=1, 0<=6 -> OK
- Test 3: pretend to grant. Available = [5, 1, 6] - [0, 1, 0] = [5, 0, 6]; Allocation[T5] = [0, 1, 3]. Now run the safety algorithm.
- Work = Available = [5, 0, 6]
- T1: Need [1, 0, 4] vs Work [5, 0, 6]: 1<=5, 0<=0, 4<=6 -> all fit, run it. Work = [5, 0, 6] + Allocation [0, 2, 2] = [5, 2, 8]
- T2: Need [0, 0, 0] vs Work [5, 2, 8]: 0<=5, 0<=2, 0<=8 -> all fit, run it. Work = [5, 2, 8] + Allocation [8, 0, 0] = [13, 2, 8]

- Resulting state is SAFE (sequence < T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6 >) -> GRANT the request

problem:
A storage trace shows the head at cylinder **216** on a 300-cylinder device, with these outstanding requests:

`207, 197, 5, 179, 103, 38, 273, 75, 163, 13, 142, 231, 76, 29`

Using **SCAN** scheduling. The head is currently moving toward higher cylinder numbers. List the order in which requests are served and compute the total distance moved.

The allocator's free list currently holds `[279, 254, 52, 139, 457, 470, 350]` KB blocks. The queue asks for `[395, 452, 122, 269, 447, 221]` KB, served first to last.

Apply **WORST-fit** allocation. Which partition serves each request?
solution:
**Policy: WORST-fit**

_Rule: take the LARGEST hole that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=279, hole 2=254, hole 3=52, hole 4=139, hole 5=457, hole 6=470, hole 7=350
- request 395: hole 1=279 < 395 no; hole 2=254 < 395 no; hole 3=52 < 395 no; hole 4=139 < 395 no; hole 5=457 >= 395 fits; hole 6=470 >= 395 fits; hole 7=350 < 395 no -> largest fitting: 470 > 457 -> hole 6; 470 - 395 = 75
- request 452: hole 1=279 < 452 no; hole 2=254 < 452 no; hole 3=52 < 452 no; hole 4=139 < 452 no; hole 5=457 >= 452 fits; hole 6=75 < 452 no; hole 7=350 < 452 no -> largest fitting: 457 -> hole 5; 457 - 452 = 5
- request 122: hole 1=279 >= 122 fits; hole 2=254 >= 122 fits; hole 3=52 < 122 no; hole 4=139 >= 122 fits; hole 5=5 < 122 no; hole 6=75 < 122 no; hole 7=350 >= 122 fits -> largest fitting: 350 > 279 > 254 > 139 -> hole 7; 350 - 122 = 228
- request 269: hole 1=279 >= 269 fits; hole 2=254 < 269 no; hole 3=52 < 269 no; hole 4=139 < 269 no; hole 5=5 < 269 no; hole 6=75 < 269 no; hole 7=228 < 269 no -> largest fitting: 279 -> hole 1; 279 - 269 = 10
- request 447: hole 1=10 < 447 no; hole 2=254 < 447 no; hole 3=52 < 447 no; hole 4=139 < 447 no; hole 5=5 < 447 no; hole 6=75 < 447 no; hole 7=228 < 447 no -> no hole fits -> must WAIT
- request 221: hole 1=10 < 221 no; hole 2=254 >= 221 fits; hole 3=52 < 221 no; hole 4=139 < 221 no; hole 5=5 < 221 no; hole 6=75 < 221 no; hole 7=228 >= 221 fits -> largest fitting: 254 > 228 -> hole 2; 254 - 221 = 33

**Placement:** 395 KB -> hole 6; 452 KB -> hole 5; 122 KB -> hole 7; 269 KB -> hole 1; 447 KB -> WAIT; 221 KB -> hole 2
**Remaining free space per hole:** [10, 33, 52, 139, 5, 75, 228]
- Sum of free space: 10 + 33 = 43, 43 + 52 = 95, 95 + 139 = 234, 234 + 5 = 239, 239 + 75 = 314, 314 + 228 = 542
**Total external fragmentation = 542 KB**

**Answer: 395 KB -> hole 6; 452 KB -> hole 5; 122 KB -> hole 7; 269 KB -> hole 1; 447 KB -> WAIT; 221 KB -> hole 2**

problem:
Here is a workload captured from a production trace:

P1 arrives at time 4 and requires 8 units of CPU time; P2 arrives at time 6 and requires 11 units of CPU time; P3 arrives at time 6 and requires 4 units of CPU time; P4 arrives at time 7 and requires 7 units of CPU time; P5 arrives at time 7 and requires 2 units of CPU time; P6 arrives at time 10 and requires 6 units of CPU time; P7 arrives at time 14 and requires 9 units of CPU time; P8 arrives at time 16 and requires 6 units of CPU time; P9 arrives at time 18 and requires 4 units of CPU time; P10 arrives at time 18 and requires 7 units of CPU time.

solution:
**Algorithm: SRTF (preemptive SJF)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: at every arrival and completion, run the ready process with the SHORTEST REMAINING time; preempt the running process if a shorter one is ready (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=4

- t=6: P2, P3 arrive; ready P3(4) < P1(6) < P2(11) -> PREEMPT P1, run P3

- t=9: P5 completes; ready P3(3) < P1(6) < P4(7) < P2(11) -> run P3
- t=10: P6 arrives; ready P3(2) < P1(6) = P6(6) < P4(7) < P2(11) -> keep running P3
- t=12: P3 completes; ready P1(6) = P6(6) < P4(7) < P2(11) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P1
- t=14: P7 arrives; ready P1(4) < P6(6) < P4(7) < P7(9) < P2(11) -> keep running P1
- t=16: P8 arrives; ready P1(2) < P6(6) = P8(6) < P4(7) < P7(9) < P2(11) -> keep running P1
- t=18: P1 completes; P9, P10 arrive; ready P9(4) < P6(6) = P8(6) < P4(7) = P10(7) < P7(9) < P2(11) -> run P9
- t=22: P9 completes; ready P6(6) = P8(6) < P4(7) = P10(7) < P7(9) < P2(11) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P6
- t=28: P6 completes; ready P8(6) < P4(7) = P10(7) < P7(9) < P2(11) -> run P8

- J3: Need [0, 1, 2, 5] vs Work [14, 10, 10, 3]: 0<=14, 1<=10, 2<=10, 5>3 -> cannot run yet
- J4: Need [0, 3, 2, 4] vs Work [14, 10, 10, 3]: 0<=14, 3<=10, 2<=10, 4>3 -> cannot run yet

**Policy: BEST-fit**

_Rule: take the SMALLEST hole that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=89, hole 2=170, hole 3=480, hole 4=215, hole 5=134, hole 6=557, hole 7=298
- request 228: hole 1=89 < 228 no; hole 2=170 < 228 no; hole 3=480 >= 228 fits; hole 4=215 < 228 no; hole 5=134 < 228 no; hole 6=557 >= 228 fits; hole 7=298 >= 228 fits -> smallest fitting: 298 < 480 < 557 -> hole 7; 298 - 228 = 70
- request 435: hole 1=89 < 435 no; hole 2=170 < 435 no; hole 3=480 >= 435 fits; hole 4=215 < 435 no; hole 5=134 < 435 no; hole 6=557 >= 435 fits; hole 7=70 < 435 no -> smallest fitting: 480 < 557 -> hole 3; 480 - 435 = 45
- request 57: hole 1=89 >= 57 fits; hole 2=170 >= 57 fits; hole 3=45 < 57 no; hole 4=215 >= 57 fits; hole 5=134 >= 57 fits; hole 6=557 >= 57 fits; hole 7=70 >= 57 fits -> smallest fitting: 70 < 89 < 134 < 170 < 215 < 557 -> hole 7; 70 - 57 = 13
- request 214: hole 1=89 < 214 no; hole 2=170 < 214 no; hole 3=45 < 214 no; hole 4=215 >= 214 fits; hole 5=134 < 214 no; hole 6=557 >= 214 fits; hole 7=13 < 214 no -> smallest fitting: 215 < 557 -> hole 4; 215 - 214 = 1
- request 75: hole 1=89 >= 75 fits; hole 2=170 >= 75 fits; hole 3=45 < 75 no; hole 4=1 < 75 no; hole 5=134 >= 75 fits; hole 6=557 >= 75 fits; hole 7=13 < 75 no -> smallest fitting: 89 < 134 < 170 < 557 -> hole 1; 89 - 75 = 14
- request 441: hole 1=14 < 441 no; hole 2=170 < 441 no; hole 3=45 < 441 no; hole 4=1 < 441 no; hole 5=134 < 441 no; hole 6=557 >= 441 fits; hole 7=13 < 441 no -> smallest fitting: 557 -> hole 6; 557 - 441 = 116

**Placement:** 228 KB -> hole 7; 435 KB -> hole 3; 57 KB -> hole 7; 214 KB -> hole 4; 75 KB -> hole 1; 441 KB -> hole 6
**Remaining free space per hole:** [14, 170, 45, 1, 134, 116, 13]
- Sum of free space: 14 + 170 = 184, 184 + 45 = 229, 229 + 1 = 230, 230 + 134 = 364, 364 + 116 = 480, 480 + 13 = 493
**Total external fragmentation = 493 KB**

**Answer: 228 KB -> hole 7; 435 KB -> hole 3; 57 KB -> hole 7; 214 KB -> hole 4; 75 KB -> hole 1; 441 KB -> hole 6**

**Algorithm: Priority (preemptive)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

- P0: [2, 6, 6, 5] - [2, 4, 4, 1] = [0, 2, 2, 4]
- P1: [0, 8, 1, 8] - [0, 6, 0, 6] = [0, 2, 1, 2]
- P2: [4, 7, 1, 4] - [3, 5, 1, 4] = [1, 2, 0, 0]
- P3: [6, 8, 4, 3] - [4, 4, 1, 3] = [2, 4, 3, 0]
- P4: [8, 3, 6, 6] - [3, 3, 0, 5] = [5, 0, 6, 1]
- P5: [3, 7, 7, 0] - [1, 4, 6, 0] = [2, 3, 1, 0]
- P6: [2, 0, 6, 7] - [2, 0, 1, 1] = [0, 0, 5, 6]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [4, 3, 3, 3]
- P0: Need [0, 2, 2, 4] vs Work [4, 3, 3, 3]: 0<=4, 2<=3, 2<=3, 4>3 -> cannot run yet
- P1: Need [0, 2, 1, 2] vs Work [4, 3, 3, 3]: 0<=4, 2<=3, 1<=3, 2<=3 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 3, 3, 3] + Allocation [0, 6, 0, 6] = [4, 9, 3, 9]
- P0: Need [0, 2, 2, 4] vs Work [4, 9, 3, 9]: 0<=4, 2<=9, 2<=3, 4<=9 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 9, 3, 9] + Allocation [2, 4, 4, 1] = [6, 13, 7, 10]
- P2: Need [1, 2, 0, 0] vs Work [6, 13, 7, 10]: 1<=6, 2<=13, 0<=7, 0<=10 -> all fit, run it. Work = [6, 13, 7, 10] + Allocation [3, 5, 1, 4] = [9, 18, 8, 14]
- P3: Need [2, 4, 3, 0] vs Work [9, 18, 8, 14]: 2<=9, 4<=18, 3<=8, 0<=14 -> all fit, run it. Work = [9, 18, 8, 14] + Allocation [4, 4, 1, 3] = [13, 22, 9, 17]
- P4: Need [5, 0, 6, 1] vs Work [13, 22, 9, 17]: 5<=13, 0<=22, 6<=9, 1<=17 -> all fit, run it. Work = [13, 22, 9, 17] + Allocation [3, 3, 0, 5] = [16, 25, 9, 22]
- P5: Need [2, 3, 1, 0] vs Work [16, 25, 9, 22]: 2<=16, 3<=25, 1<=9, 0<=22 -> all fit, run it. Work = [16, 25, 9, 22] + Allocation [1, 4, 6, 0] = [17, 29, 15, 22]
- P6: Need [0, 0, 5, 6] vs Work [17, 29, 15, 22]: 0<=17, 0<=29, 5<=15, 6<=22 -> all fit, run it. Work = [17, 29, 15, 22] + Allocation [2, 0, 1, 1] = [19, 29, 16, 23]

**Step 3 - conclusion**

All 7 processes can complete, so the system is in a **SAFE state**.
A safe sequence is **< P1, P0, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6 >**.

_Safe sequences are not unique: any ordering in which each process's Need is met by the running Work vector is equally correct._

**Answer: SAFE, safe sequence < P1, P0, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6 >**

problem:
Address-translation hardware uses 4096-byte pages and this mapping:

| Page | Frame |
|------|-------|
| 0    | 47    |
| 1    | 52    |
| 2    | 1     |
| 3    | 36    |
| 4    | 32    |
| 5    | 60    |
| 6    | 3     |
| 7    | 60    |
| 8    | 42    |
| 9    | 4     |
| 10   | 31    |
| 11   | 13    |
| 12   | 54    |
| 13   | 5     |

Compute the physical address for logical address **39644**.
solution:
**Step-by-step translation**

- page number = floor(39644 / 4096) = 9  (check: 9 x 4096 = 36864 <= 39644 < 40960)
- page offset = 39644 - 36864 = 2780
- page table[9] = frame 4
- frame base = 4 x 4096 = 16384
- physical address = 16384 + 2780 = 19164

**Physical address = 19164**

**Answer: physical address = 19164**

Use **SJF (non-preemptive)**. Draw the Gantt chart showing the execution order.

An allocation snapshot from a 4-resource system (A, B, C, D) with 7 processes: Free instances right now: [2, 5, 0, 2].

| P  | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Alloc D | Max A | Max B | Max C | Max D |
|----|---------|---------|---------|---------|-------|-------|-------|-------|
| J1 | 3       | 1       | 0       | 3       | 8     | 2     | 0     | 4     |
| J2 | 4       | 0       | 0       | 0       | 4     | 5     | 0     | 0     |
| J3 | 0       | 3       | 0       | 3       | 2     | 8     | 0     | 5     |
| J4 | 0       | 3       | 1       | 1       | 0     | 5     | 6     | 7     |
| J5 | 0       | 0       | 2       | 6       | 8     | 1     | 5     | 7     |
| J6 | 7       | 0       | 7       | 0       | 8     | 0     | 8     | 2     |
| J7 | 1       | 1       | 2       | 5       | 4     | 2     | 5     | 5     |

Is this state safe? Apply the safety algorithm and show a safe sequence if one exists.
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C, D)

- J1: [8, 2, 0, 4] - [3, 1, 0, 3] = [5, 1, 0, 1]
- J2: [4, 5, 0, 0] - [4, 0, 0, 0] = [0, 5, 0, 0]
- J3: [2, 8, 0, 5] - [0, 3, 0, 3] = [2, 5, 0, 2]
- J4: [0, 5, 6, 7] - [0, 3, 1, 1] = [0, 2, 5, 6]
- J5: [8, 1, 5, 7] - [0, 0, 2, 6] = [8, 1, 3, 1]
- J6: [8, 0, 8, 2] - [7, 0, 7, 0] = [1, 0, 1, 2]
- J7: [4, 2, 5, 5] - [1, 1, 2, 5] = [3, 1, 3, 0]

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [2, 5, 0, 2]
- J1: Need [5, 1, 0, 1] vs Work [2, 5, 0, 2]: 5>2, 1<=5, 0<=0, 1<=2 -> cannot run yet
- J2: Need [0, 5, 0, 0] vs Work [2, 5, 0, 2]: 0<=2, 5<=5, 0<=0, 0<=2 -> all fit, run it. Work = [2, 5, 0, 2] + Allocation [4, 0, 0, 0] = [6, 5, 0, 2]
- J1: Need [5, 1, 0, 1] vs Work [6, 5, 0, 2]: 5<=6, 1<=5, 0<=0, 1<=2 -> all fit, run it. Work = [6, 5, 0, 2] + Allocation [3, 1, 0, 3] = [9, 6, 0, 5]
- J3: Need [2, 5, 0, 2] vs Work [9, 6, 0, 5]: 2<=9, 5<=6, 0<=0, 2<=5 -> all fit, run it. Work = [9, 6, 0, 5] + Allocation [0, 3, 0, 3] = [9, 9, 0, 8]
- J4: Need [0, 2, 5, 6] vs Work [9, 9, 0, 8]: 0<=9, 2<=9, 5>0, 6<=8 -> cannot run yet
- J5: Need [8, 1, 3, 1] vs Work [9, 9, 0, 8]: 8<=9, 1<=9, 3>0, 1<=8 -> cannot run yet
- J6: Need [1, 0, 1, 2] vs Work [9, 9, 0, 8]: 1<=9, 0<=9, 1>0, 2<=8 -> cannot run yet
- J7: Need [3, 1, 3, 0] vs Work [9, 9, 0, 8]: 3<=9, 1<=9, 3>0, 0<=8 -> cannot run yet

**Step 3 - conclusion**

No remaining process (J4, J5, J6, J7) has a Need that fits in Work [9, 9, 0, 8], so they can never all finish: the system is **NOT in a safe state (UNSAFE)**. Processes J2, J1, J3 could finish, but J4, J5, J6, J7 cannot.

_Unsafe does not mean deadlocked yet: it means a deadlock is possible if the processes request their maximum._

**Answer: UNSAFE, no safe sequence exists**

problem:
Reproduce the following schedule from last term's exam paper:

| Process | Arrival | Burst |
|---------|---------|-------|
| P1      | 0       | 10    |
| P2      | 3       | 2     |
| P3      | 6       | 12    |
| P4      | 6       | 12    |
| P5      | 9       | 5     |
| P6      | 10      | 3     |
| P7      | 14      | 3     |
| P8      | 14      | 6     |
| P9      | 15      | 11    |
| P10     | 19      | 2     |

They are scheduled with **SRTF (preemptive SJF)**. Show the schedule step by step and report both averages.
solution:
**Algorithm: SRTF (preemptive SJF)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: at every arrival and completion, run the ready process with the SHORTEST REMAINING time; preempt the running process if a shorter one is ready (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: P1 arrives; only P1 is ready -> run P1
- t=3: P2 arrives; ready P2(2) < P1(7) -> PREEMPT P1, run P2
- t=5: P2 completes; only P1 is ready -> run P1
- t=6: P3, P4 arrive; ready P1(6) < P3(12) = P4(12) -> keep running P1
- t=9: P5 arrives; ready P1(3) < P5(5) < P3(12) = P4(12) -> keep running P1
- t=10: P6 arrives; ready P1(2) < P6(3) < P5(5) < P3(12) = P4(12) -> keep running P1
- t=12: P1 completes; ready P6(3) < P5(5) < P3(12) = P4(12) -> run P6
- t=14: P7, P8 arrive; ready P6(1) < P7(3) < P5(5) < P8(6) < P3(12) = P4(12) -> keep running P6
- t=15: P6 completes; P9 arrives; ready P7(3) < P5(5) < P8(6) < P9(11) < P3(12) = P4(12) -> run P7
- t=18: P7 completes; ready P5(5) < P8(6) < P9(11) < P3(12) = P4(12) -> run P5
- t=19: P10 arrives; ready P10(2) < P5(4) < P8(6) < P9(11) < P3(12) = P4(12) -> PREEMPT P5, run P10
- t=21: P10 completes; ready P5(4) < P8(6) < P9(11) < P3(12) = P4(12) -> run P5
- t=25: P5 completes; ready P8(6) < P9(11) < P3(12) = P4(12) -> run P8
- t=31: P8 completes; ready P9(11) < P3(12) = P4(12) -> run P9
- t=42: P9 completes; ready P3(12) = P4(12) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P3
- t=54: P3 completes; only P4 is ready -> run P4
- t=66: P4 completes; all processes done

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** P1[0-3] P2[3-5] P1[5-12] P6[12-15] P7[15-18] P5[18-19] P10[19-21] P5[21-25] P8[25-31] P9[31-42] P3[42-54] P4[54-66]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround   | Waiting      |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|--------------|--------------|
| P1      | 0       | 10    | 12         | 12 - 0 = 12  | 12 - 10 = 2  |
| P10     | 19      | 2     | 21         | 21 - 19 = 2  | 2 - 2 = 0    |
| P2      | 3       | 2     | 5          | 5 - 3 = 2    | 2 - 2 = 0    |
| P3      | 6       | 12    | 54         | 54 - 6 = 48  | 48 - 12 = 36 |
| P4      | 6       | 12    | 66         | 66 - 6 = 60  | 60 - 12 = 48 |

**Step 2 - run the safety algorithm** (scan the processes in order; run the first one whose Need fits in Work, then add its Allocation to Work and scan again)

- Work = Available = [4, 2, 2, 5]
- P1: Need [0, 0, 4, 0] vs Work [4, 2, 2, 5]: 0<=4, 0<=2, 4>2, 0<=5 -> cannot run yet
- P2: Need [2, 0, 0, 0] vs Work [4, 2, 2, 5]: 2<=4, 0<=2, 0<=2, 0<=5 -> all fit, run it. Work = [4, 2, 2, 5] + Allocation [6, 3, 0, 0] = [10, 5, 2, 5]

- P3: Need [0, 2, 2, 5] vs Work [10, 5, 2, 5]: 0<=10, 2<=5, 2<=2, 5<=5 -> all fit, run it. Work = [10, 5, 2, 5] + Allocation [2, 0, 3, 2] = [12, 5, 5, 7]
- P1: Need [0, 0, 4, 0] vs Work [12, 5, 5, 7]: 0<=12, 0<=5, 4<=5, 0<=7 -> all fit, run it. Work = [12, 5, 5, 7] + Allocation [3, 5, 0, 5] = [15, 10, 5, 12]
- P4: Need [1, 3, 7, 1] vs Work [15, 10, 5, 12]: 1<=15, 3<=10, 7>5, 1<=12 -> cannot run yet
- P5: Need [0, 1, 0, 3] vs Work [15, 10, 5, 12]: 0<=15, 1<=10, 0<=5, 3<=12 -> all fit, run it. Work = [15, 10, 5, 12] + Allocation [3, 4, 5, 4] = [18, 14, 10, 16]
- P4: Need [1, 3, 7, 1] vs Work [18, 14, 10, 16]: 1<=18, 3<=14, 7<=10, 1<=16 -> all fit, run it. Work = [18, 14, 10, 16] + Allocation [2, 5, 0, 2] = [20, 19, 10, 18]

All 7 processes can complete, so the system is in a **SAFE state**.

problem:

**Algorithm: Priority (preemptive)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: at every arrival and completion, run the ready process with the HIGHEST priority (LOWEST number); preempt the running process if a higher-priority one is ready (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=2
- t=2: P1 arrives; only P1 is ready -> run P1
- t=4: P2 arrives; ready P1(p1) < P2(p2) -> keep running P1
- t=5: P1 completes; only P2 is ready -> run P2
- t=7: P2 completes; no process ready -> CPU idle until t=8
- t=8: P3 arrives; only P3 is ready -> run P3
- t=9: P3 completes; no process ready -> CPU idle until t=14
- t=14: P4 arrives; only P4 is ready -> run P4
- t=15: P4 completes; no process ready -> CPU idle until t=18
- t=18: P5 arrives; only P5 is ready -> run P5
- t=20: P6 arrives; ready P6(p2) < P5(p5) -> PREEMPT P5, run P6
- t=24: P6 completes; only P5 is ready -> run P5
- t=26: P5 completes; P7 arrives; only P7 is ready -> run P7
- t=30: P7 completes; no process ready -> CPU idle until t=31
