- t=36: P9 arrives; ready P8(p1) < P9(p4) -> keep running P8
- t=37: P10 arrives; ready P8(p1) < P10(p2) < P9(p4) -> keep running P8
- t=41: P8 completes; ready P10(p2) < P9(p4) -> run P10
- t=45: P10 completes; only P9 is ready -> run P9
- t=57: P9 completes; all processes done

| P1      | 2       | 3     | 5          | 5 - 2 = 3    | 3 - 3 = 0   |

| P7      | 26      | 4     | 30         | 30 - 26 = 4  | 4 - 4 = 0   |
| P8      | 31      | 10    | 41         | 41 - 31 = 10 | 10 - 10 = 0 |
| P9      | 36      | 12    | 57         | 57 - 36 = 21 | 21 - 12 = 9 |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 0 + 4 = 4, 4 + 1 = 5, 5 + 0 = 5, 5 + 0 = 5, 5 + 4 = 9, 9 + 0 = 9, 9 + 0 = 9, 9 + 0 = 9, 9 + 9 = 18

- Sum of turnaround times: 3 + 8 = 11, 11 + 3 = 14, 14 + 1 = 15, 15 + 1 = 16, 16 + 8 = 24, 24 + 4 = 28, 28 + 4 = 32, 32 + 10 = 42, 42 + 21 = 63
- Average turnaround time = 63 / 10 = **6.3**

- P4: Need [6, 4, 5] vs Work [4, 4, 1]: 6>4, 4<=4, 5>1 -> cannot run yet

- P2: Need [1, 0, 7] vs Work [8, 9, 2]: 1<=8, 0<=9, 7>2 -> cannot run yet
- P3: Need [0, 5, 0] vs Work [8, 9, 2]: 0<=8, 5<=9, 0<=2 -> all fit, run it. Work = [8, 9, 2] + Allocation [5, 2, 1] = [13, 11, 3]

- P4: Need [6, 4, 5] vs Work [16, 14, 5]: 6<=16, 4<=14, 5<=5 -> all fit, run it. Work = [16, 14, 5] + Allocation [0, 1, 2] = [16, 15, 7]

problem:
The following state was dumped by a resource monitor (3 types: A, B, C, 6 processes): The monitor reports [5, 5, 6] units still unallocated.

| P  | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Max A | Max B | Max C |
|----|---------|---------|---------|-------|-------|-------|
| P0 | 1       | 0       | 3       | 5     | 6     | 7     |
| P1 | 3       | 0       | 1       | 5     | 3     | 8     |
| P2 | 0       | 0       | 1       | 3     | 5     | 1     |
| P3 | 1       | 0       | 1       | 8     | 1     | 1     |
| P4 | 1       | 6       | 5       | 3     | 7     | 7     |
| P5 | 5       | 3       | 1       | 8     | 6     | 3     |

Process P0 now requests [0, 5, 0]. Should this request be granted?
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C)

- P0: [5, 6, 7] - [1, 0, 3] = [4, 6, 4]
- P1: [5, 3, 8] - [3, 0, 1] = [2, 3, 7]
- P2: [3, 5, 1] - [0, 0, 1] = [3, 5, 0]
- P3: [8, 1, 1] - [1, 0, 1] = [7, 1, 0]
- P4: [3, 7, 7] - [1, 6, 5] = [2, 1, 2]
- P5: [8, 6, 3] - [5, 3, 1] = [3, 3, 2]

**Step 2 - apply the three tests of the resource-request algorithm**

- Test 1: Request [0, 5, 0] vs Need [4, 6, 4]: 0<=4, 5<=6, 0<=4 -> OK
- Test 2: Request [0, 5, 0] vs Available [5, 5, 6]: 0<=5, 5<=5, 0<=6 -> OK
- Test 3: pretend to grant. Available = [5, 5, 6] - [0, 5, 0] = [5, 0, 6]; Allocation[P0] = [1, 5, 3]. Now run the safety algorithm.
- Work = Available = [5, 0, 6]
- P0: Need [4, 1, 4] vs Work [5, 0, 6]: 4<=5, 1>0, 4<=6 -> cannot run yet
- P1: Need [2, 3, 7] vs Work [5, 0, 6]: 2<=5, 3>0, 7>6 -> cannot run yet
- P2: Need [3, 5, 0] vs Work [5, 0, 6]: 3<=5, 5>0, 0<=6 -> cannot run yet
- P3: Need [7, 1, 0] vs Work [5, 0, 6]: 7>5, 1>0, 0<=6 -> cannot run yet
- P4: Need [2, 1, 2] vs Work [5, 0, 6]: 2<=5, 1>0, 2<=6 -> cannot run yet
- P5: Need [3, 3, 2] vs Work [5, 0, 6]: 3<=5, 3>0, 2<=6 -> cannot run yet
- UNSAFE - no safe sequence exists; processes P0, P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 can never finish
- Resulting state is UNSAFE -> DENY the request; P0 must wait and the old state is restored

**Conclusion: the request is DENIED.**

**Answer: DENIED**

problem:
Reproduce the following schedule from last term's exam paper:

- **P1**: arrives at t=1, needs 8 ms of CPU, priority 5
- **P2**: arrives at t=4, needs 10 ms of CPU, priority 1
- **P3**: arrives at t=8, needs 1 ms of CPU, priority 5
- **P4**: arrives at t=8, needs 1 ms of CPU, priority 5
- **P5**: arrives at t=12, needs 12 ms of CPU, priority 2
- **P6**: arrives at t=12, needs 2 ms of CPU, priority 1
- **P7**: arrives at t=14, needs 6 ms of CPU, priority 3

The scheduler uses **Priority (preemptive)** (a lower number means higher priority). What is the average waiting time?
solution:
**Algorithm: Priority (preemptive)**

**Step 1 - build the schedule**

_Rule: at every arrival and completion, run the ready process with the HIGHEST priority (LOWEST number); preempt the running process if a higher-priority one is ready (ties: earlier arrival, then name)._

- t=0: no process has arrived -> CPU idle until t=1
- t=1: P1 arrives; only P1 is ready -> run P1
- t=4: P2 arrives; ready P2(p1) < P1(p5) -> PREEMPT P1, run P2
- t=8: P3, P4 arrive; ready P2(p1) < P1(p5) = P3(p5) = P4(p5) -> keep running P2
- t=12: P5, P6 arrive; ready P2(p1) = P6(p1) < P5(p2) < P1(p5) = P3(p5) = P4(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> keep running P2
- t=14: P2 completes; P7 arrives; ready P6(p1) < P5(p2) < P7(p3) < P1(p5) = P3(p5) = P4(p5) -> run P6
- t=16: P6 completes; ready P5(p2) < P7(p3) < P1(p5) = P3(p5) = P4(p5) -> run P5
- t=28: P5 completes; ready P7(p3) < P1(p5) = P3(p5) = P4(p5) -> run P7
- t=34: P7 completes; ready P1(p5) = P3(p5) = P4(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P1
- t=39: P1 completes; ready P3(p5) = P4(p5) (tie -> earlier arrival, then name) -> run P3
- t=40: P3 completes; only P4 is ready -> run P4
- t=41: P4 completes; all processes done

**Step 2 - Gantt chart:** P1[1-4] P2[4-14] P6[14-16] P5[16-28] P7[28-34] P1[34-39] P3[39-40] P4[40-41]

**Step 3 - per-process times** (Turnaround = Completion - Arrival; Waiting = Turnaround - Burst)

| Process | Arrival | Burst | Completion | Turnaround   | Waiting     |
|---------|---------|-------|------------|--------------|-------------|
| P1      | 1       | 8     | 39         | 39 - 1 = 38  | 38 - 8 = 30 |
| P2      | 4       | 10    | 14         | 14 - 4 = 10  | 10 - 10 = 0 |
| P3      | 8       | 1     | 40         | 40 - 8 = 32  | 32 - 1 = 31 |
| P4      | 8       | 1     | 41         | 41 - 8 = 33  | 33 - 1 = 32 |
| P5      | 12      | 12    | 28         | 28 - 12 = 16 | 16 - 12 = 4 |
| P6      | 12      | 2     | 16         | 16 - 12 = 4  | 4 - 2 = 2   |
| P7      | 14      | 6     | 34         | 34 - 14 = 20 | 20 - 6 = 14 |

**Step 4 - averages**

- Sum of waiting times: 30 + 0 = 30, 30 + 31 = 61, 61 + 32 = 93, 93 + 4 = 97, 97 + 2 = 99, 99 + 14 = 113
- Average waiting time = 113 / 7 = **16.14**
- Sum of turnaround times: 38 + 10 = 48, 48 + 32 = 80, 80 + 33 = 113, 113 + 16 = 129, 129 + 4 = 133, 133 + 20 = 153
- Average turnaround time = 153 / 7 = **21.86**

**Answer: average waiting time = 16.14**

problem:
The following state was dumped by a resource monitor (3 types: A, B, C, 7 processes): The monitor reports [1, 3, 2] units still unallocated.

| P  | Alloc A | Alloc B | Alloc C | Max A | Max B | Max C |
|----|---------|---------|---------|-------|-------|-------|
| J1 | 7       | 2       | 6       | 7     | 2     | 8     |
| J2 | 1       | 2       | 0       | 5     | 3     | 0     |
| J3 | 4       | 2       | 5       | 5     | 6     | 5     |
| J4 | 2       | 1       | 0       | 3     | 3     | 0     |
| J5 | 1       | 0       | 3       | 4     | 3     | 8     |
| J6 | 0       | 0       | 0       | 5     | 7     | 7     |
| J7 | 0       | 2       | 3       | 1     | 7     | 4     |

Using the resource-request algorithm, determine whether J6's request for [0, 1, 1] can be granted.
solution:
**Step 1 - compute Need = Max - Allocation, row by row** (resources A, B, C)

- J1: [7, 2, 8] - [7, 2, 6] = [0, 0, 2]
- J2: [5, 3, 0] - [1, 2, 0] = [4, 1, 0]
- J3: [5, 6, 5] - [4, 2, 5] = [1, 4, 0]
- J4: [3, 3, 0] - [2, 1, 0] = [1, 2, 0]
- J5: [4, 3, 8] - [1, 0, 3] = [3, 3, 5]
- J6: [5, 7, 7] - [0, 0, 0] = [5, 7, 7]
- J7: [1, 7, 4] - [0, 2, 3] = [1, 5, 1]

**Step 2 - apply the three tests of the resource-request algorithm**

- Test 1: Request [0, 1, 1] vs Need [5, 7, 7]: 0<=5, 1<=7, 1<=7 -> OK
- Test 2: Request [0, 1, 1] vs Available [1, 3, 2]: 0<=1, 1<=3, 1<=2 -> OK
- Test 3: pretend to grant. Available = [1, 3, 2] - [0, 1, 1] = [1, 2, 1]; Allocation[J6] = [0, 1, 1]. Now run the safety algorithm.
- Work = Available = [1, 2, 1]
- J1: Need [0, 0, 2] vs Work [1, 2, 1]: 0<=1, 0<=2, 2>1 -> cannot run yet
- J2: Need [4, 1, 0] vs Work [1, 2, 1]: 4>1, 1<=2, 0<=1 -> cannot run yet
- J3: Need [1, 4, 0] vs Work [1, 2, 1]: 1<=1, 4>2, 0<=1 -> cannot run yet
- J4: Need [1, 2, 0] vs Work [1, 2, 1]: 1<=1, 2<=2, 0<=1 -> all fit, run it. Work = [1, 2, 1] + Allocation [2, 1, 0] = [3, 3, 1]
- J1: Need [0, 0, 2] vs Work [3, 3, 1]: 0<=3, 0<=3, 2>1 -> cannot run yet
- J2: Need [4, 1, 0] vs Work [3, 3, 1]: 4>3, 1<=3, 0<=1 -> cannot run yet
- J3: Need [1, 4, 0] vs Work [3, 3, 1]: 1<=3, 4>3, 0<=1 -> cannot run yet
- J5: Need [3, 3, 5] vs Work [3, 3, 1]: 3<=3, 3<=3, 5>1 -> cannot run yet
- J6: Need [5, 6, 6] vs Work [3, 3, 1]: 5>3, 6>3, 6>1 -> cannot run yet
- J7: Need [1, 5, 1] vs Work [3, 3, 1]: 1<=3, 5>3, 1<=1 -> cannot run yet
- UNSAFE - no safe sequence exists; processes J1, J2, J3, J5, J6, J7 can never finish
- Resulting state is UNSAFE -> DENY the request; J6 must wait and the old state is restored

**Conclusion: the request is DENIED.**

**Answer: DENIED**

Convert logical address **1134** into its physical equivalent, showing the page number and offset.
solution:
**Step-by-step translation**

- page number = floor(1134 / 4096) = 0  (check: 0 x 4096 = 0 <= 1134 < 4096)

- page table[0] = frame 53

problem:
The allocator's free list currently holds `[481, 456, 373, 185, 230, 497]` KB blocks. Pending requests, in arrival order: `[262, 120, 292, 349, 128]` KB.

Apply **WORST-fit** allocation. Which partition serves each request?
solution:
**Policy: WORST-fit**

_Rule: take the LARGEST hole that is large enough; the leftover stays as a smaller hole. A request that fits nowhere must wait._

- holes (free KB, numbered in order): hole 1=481, hole 2=456, hole 3=373, hole 4=185, hole 5=230, hole 6=497
- request 262: hole 1=481 >= 262 fits; hole 2=456 >= 262 fits; hole 3=373 >= 262 fits; hole 4=185 < 262 no; hole 5=230 < 262 no; hole 6=497 >= 262 fits -> largest fitting: 497 > 481 > 456 > 373 -> hole 6; 497 - 262 = 235
- request 120: hole 1=481 >= 120 fits; hole 2=456 >= 120 fits; hole 3=373 >= 120 fits; hole 4=185 >= 120 fits; hole 5=230 >= 120 fits; hole 6=235 >= 120 fits -> largest fitting: 481 > 456 > 373 > 235 > 230 > 185 -> hole 1; 481 - 120 = 361
- request 292: hole 1=361 >= 292 fits; hole 2=456 >= 292 fits; hole 3=373 >= 292 fits; hole 4=185 < 292 no; hole 5=230 < 292 no; hole 6=235 < 292 no -> largest fitting: 456 > 373 > 361 -> hole 2; 456 - 292 = 164
- request 349: hole 1=361 >= 349 fits; hole 2=164 < 349 no; hole 3=373 >= 349 fits; hole 4=185 < 349 no; hole 5=230 < 349 no; hole 6=235 < 349 no -> largest fitting: 373 > 361 -> hole 3; 373 - 349 = 24
- request 128: hole 1=361 >= 128 fits; hole 2=164 >= 128 fits; hole 3=24 < 128 no; hole 4=185 >= 128 fits; hole 5=230 >= 128 fits; hole 6=235 >= 128 fits -> largest fitting: 361 > 235 > 230 > 185 > 164 -> hole 1; 361 - 128 = 233

**Placement:** 262 KB -> hole 6; 120 KB -> hole 1; 292 KB -> hole 2; 349 KB -> hole 3; 128 KB -> hole 1
**Remaining free space per hole:** [233, 164, 24, 185, 230, 235]
- Sum of free space: 233 + 164 = 397, 397 + 24 = 421, 421 + 185 = 606, 606 + 230 = 836, 836 + 235 = 1071
**Total external fragmentation = 1071 KB**

**Answer: 262 KB -> hole 6; 120 KB -> hole 1; 292 KB -> hole 2; 349 KB -> hole 3; 128 KB -> hole 1**
